articles.title: Peyton Watson to Cavs in 5-Team Trade, Full Return for Nuggets, Clippers and New Rumors on Contract
articles.summary: Peyton Watson's standoff with the Denver Nuggets is over after they agreed to a sign-and-trade involving the Cleveland Cavaliers, Los Angeles Clippers and more, the Nuggets confirmed Thursday.
articles.body:
Peyton Watson's standoff with the Denver Nuggets is over after they agreed to a sign-and-trade involving the Cleveland Cavaliers, Los Angeles Clippers and more, the Nuggets confirmed Thursday.

Denver is trading Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers and will receive Cleveland's 2031 first-round pick and a 2032 second-rounder from the Sacramento Kings. The Cavs are sending Max Strus to the Los Angeles Clippers, which gives them the flexibility to sign Watson to a four-year, $88 million contract.

There were multiple other minor moves involved to complete the deal, including the Washington Wizards and Charlotte Hornets:

Here is a full look at the new pieces of the blockbuster trade, plus Charlotte's inclusion with the previously reported Dennis Schroder trade.

Once the move is official, the Cavaliers can re-sign James Harden, according to NBA reporter Marc Stein .

This trade also brings an end to Watson's long saga of restricted free agency.

It was the double-edged sword of Watson turning a corner and becoming a valuable secondary piece for Denver. The better he performed, the higher his price tag eventually climbed this summer.

The 23-year-old is coming off the best season of his career, though it came to a premature end thanks to a hamstring injury.

In 54 appearances, he averaged 14.6 points and 4.9 rebounds. While his per-game production coincided with a bump in his playing time, he also had his highest true shooting percentage (59.4) ever, per Basketball Reference .

Watson's three-point shooting jumped from 35.3 percent to 41.1 percent.

His top showing came in a January win over the Washington Wizards. He finished with 35 points, eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and four blocks in 40 minutes on the floor.

NBA insider Jake Fischer reported in April that the Los Angeles Lakers, Chicago Bulls and Brooklyn Nets were all potential landing spots for Watson, and his market was bound to grow once the offseason kicked into gear.

A player as young as Watson and who possesses his skill set is a valuable commodity on the open market. His value got a boost from the fact that there weren't a lot of stars in the 2026 free-agent class, either.

Jalen Duren's stock took a hit during the playoffs, and he's likewise a restricted free agent. LeBron James and James Harden are both deep into their careers and aren't good long-term investments.

For the few teams that had a lot of spending flexibility, Watson was likely at or near the top of their wish list.

His free agency dragged on much longer than expected, probably due to his RFA status. Prospective suitors knew the Nuggets would likely match a reasonable contract offer. Precluding that scenario meant giving up additional assets in a sign-and-trade on top of tabling a big deal, maybe a combination of the two.

More surprising was Denver's approach to Watson as the team played serious hardball. Either the front office believes his 2025-26 improvement was a bit of a fluke, or it didn't think the cap implications of re-signing him were worth it.

Maybe that broad assessment proves true.

In the immediate term, the Nuggets are taking a step backward as there's no straightforward way to replicate Watson's impact on the floor.

For the Cavs, an addition of this significance looked unattainable once James chose the Philadelphia 76ers. Cleveland is well over the cap before accounting for the cost of re-signing James Harden.

Watson is a big upgrade at the 3 over Strus and gives coach Kenny Atkinson a little more depth in the frontcourt. He can fit as a small-ball 4 when Atkinson wants to give Evan Mobley some rest or deploy Mobley at center.

This acquisition doesn't make the Cavaliers the clear favorites in the East but does achieve the aim of strengthening a roster that clearly wasn't up to par last year.

Bobby Marks of ESPN provided details on the salary caps:

As Marks notes, neither the Cavs nor the Nuggets have tradeable first-round draft picks available.

The sign-and-trade for Watson comes after the 23-year-old posted 14.6 points, 4.9 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game across 54 contests. He shot 49.1 percent from the field and 41.1 percent from deep.

While he played a big role for Denver while Aaron Gordon and Christian Braun were out with injuries, Watson also dealt with a lingering hamstring injury that led to him missing significant time.

Nonetheless, the former first-rounder had the best season of his career, and it led to a big payday.

Strus is coming off an injury-riddled season that saw him play just 12 games, not making his season debut until March. Now with the Clippers, he'll look to return to being an impactful starter.

Having secured Watson, who will presumably take over as the starting small forward, the next task for Cleveland is to sign James Harden. While Harden is a free agent, all signs point to him returning to the Cavs, and a new deal for him reportedly could come soon.

articles.title: New DeMar DeRozan Rumors Reveal Potential Landing Spot After Peyton Watson Trade to Cavs
articles.summary: The Denver Nuggets reportedly are eyeing a veteran All-Star after trading Peyton Watson on Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Denver Nuggets reportedly are eyeing a veteran All-Star after trading Peyton Watson on Wednesday.

Per NBA insider Chris Haynes, the Nuggets "have their eyes on" DeMar DeRozan, who is a free agent following his release from the Sacramento Kings earlier this offseason.

The potential move comes amid a tough salary cap constraint for Denver:

While the 37-year-old DeRozan is far past his prime, he could surely still make an impact on the Nuggets. Last season, he put up 18.4 points, 4.1 assists and 2.9 rebounds per game for the Kings.

Perhaps DeRozan's most impressive stat is that he's played 74 or more games in each of the last five years. That kind of durability is rare in the NBA, especially for an aging player.

Denver is hoping to stay relevant in a competitive Western Conference, and a player like DeRozan is bound to give it a much-needed boost on offense.

But the Nuggets will have some competition in the race for DeRozan, as the Washington Wizards and the Miami Heat reportedly have interest in him as well. All three options could be intriguing for DeRozan depending on what he's looking for at this point in his career.

In Denver, he'd get to play alongside Nikola Jokić, who makes everyone around him better, and that roster would surely be able to make a run in the West.

In Washington, he'd get to team up with Anthony Davis, Trae Young and AJ Dybantsa on a young team that could make noise in the East.

Miami would give DeRozan the chance to play with Giannis Antetokounmpo after he was traded this offseason. DeRozan, Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo would at least be able to give the stacked Eastern Conference a little bit of trouble.

Where DeRozan will end up remains to be seen, but he's still after his first championship, and his desire to win a title will surely motivate his decision.

articles.title: Enrevesado traspaso NBA entre cinco equipos: Peyton Watson y Strus, los nombres más sonados
articles.standfirst: Denver traspasaría a Watson a los Cavaliers como parte de un acuerdo a tres bandas que incluía a los Clippers. El traspaso se amplió a cuatro equipos con los Wizards (operación de Tre Mann) y a cinco con el traspaso de Schröder a de los Cavs a los Hornets
articles.summary: Denver traspasaría a Watson a los Cavaliers como parte de un acuerdo a tres bandas que incluía a los Clippers. El traspaso se amplió a cuatro equipos con los Wizards (operación de Tre Mann) y a cinco con el traspaso de Schröder a de los Cavs a los Hornets
articles.body: La cadena ESPN adelanta que Cavaliers, Nuggets y Clippers han acordado un traspaso que enviará a Peyton Watson a Cleveland y a Max Strus a Los Ángeles. Shams Charania informa que como parte del acuerdo entre varios equipos, Denver recibirá una elección de primera ronda de los Cavs de 2031 sin protección y una elección de segunda ronda de los Sacramento Kings de 2032. Watson firmará un nuevo contrato de cuatro años y 88 millones de dólares —que incluye una opción de jugador y una cláusula de bonificación por traspaso— para unirse a los Cavaliers. La pasada temporada promedió 14,6 puntos, 4,9 rebotes y 2,1 asistencias. En la última semana, los Cavs han traspasado a Dennis Schroder a los Charlotte Hornets a cambio de Tre Mann, y ahora han sumado la salida de Strus. La operación de Schroder, realizada el viernes pasado, convierte este intercambio global en un acuerdo entre cinco equipos. Los Clippers envían a Cleveland una elección de segunda ronda del draft de 2027 —obtenida de los Philadelphia 76ers en el traspaso de Johni Broome— para hacerse con un jugador consolidado como Strus mediante una excepción de traspaso. Como parte del acuerdo, los Cavaliers envían a Mann, la elección de segunda ronda de 2027 de los Clippers y una compensación económica a los Washington Wizards a cambio de Cam Whitmore. Los Wizards también envían a Julian Reese a los Nuggets, quienes prescindirán de él (cortarán su contrato) tras su acuerdo de 'two-way contract'.

articles.title: Se suman antagonistas contra la "MAGA Barbie" en la WNBA: "Hay que proteger a los niños trans"
articles.standfirst: "No quiero darles más relevancia de la que merecen", declaró Cheryl Reeve (Minnesota Lynx) sobre las manifestaciones de 'Salven el deporte femenino'
articles.summary: "No quiero darles más relevancia de la que merecen", declaró Cheryl Reeve (Minnesota Lynx) sobre las manifestaciones de 'Salven el deporte femenino'
articles.body: Las entrenadoras Cheryl Reeve (Minnesota Lynx) y Natalie Nakase (Golden State Valkyries) se han pronunciado contra las manifestaciones 'Save Women's Sports» (Salven el deporte femenino)' de apoyo a la postura de Sophie Cunningham, que está en contra de las deportistas transgénero compitiendo en el deporte femenino. 'Yahoo Sports' destaca que desde las declaraciones iniciales de Cunningham sobre la protección del deporte femenino, se han celebrado cerca de siete manifestaciones en su apoyo, incluida una durante el partido entre Valkyries y Lynx. La manifestación en el Scotiabank Arena de Toronto estuvo liderada por la atleta canadiense April Hutchinson. La participación de deportistas transgénero en el deporte femenino se ha convertido en un tema cada vez más politizado en Estados Unidos; recientemente, la Corte Suprema respaldó las prohibiciones estatales que impiden a los deportistas trans competir junto a deportistas cisgénero. El fallo se produjo aproximadamente un año después de que el presidente Donald Trump emitiera una orden ejecutiva para intentar impedir que los atletas trans compitieran en deportes femeninos. Sophie Cunningham, a la que han bautizado como "MAGA (Make America Great Again) Barbie", destacó la importancia del Título IX, una ley de igualdad de género aprobada en 1972 que prohíbe la discriminación por sexo en programas educativos que reciben fondos federales. A esta ley pionera se le atribuye haber aumentado exponencialmente la participación de niñas y mujeres en el deporte en Estados Unidos. "Por eso existe el Título IX. Por eso tenemos a algunas de las grandes figuras del deporte femenino. Si el Título IX y el deporte femenino no estuvieran protegidos, no oiríamos hablar de mujeres en el deporte. Por eso creo que es realmente importante protegerlo en el futuro". Preguntada sobre esas manifestaciones Cheryl Reeve, entrenadora de las Lynx, contestó que "no quiero darles más relevancia de la que merecen". La entrenadora de las Lynx sostiene que "como ya he dicho antes, los niños transgénero tienen su lugar; creo que, tal como estamos viendo en el panorama político de este país, han encontrado un argumento que la gente está comprando. Lo único que pido es que la gente se informe mejor sobre estos temas y sobre lo que somos capaces de lograr cuando trabajamos juntos en algo, y que eso no se utilice simplemente como retórica para marginar a una comunidad que no merece ser marginada". "Tenemos que proteger a los niños trans. Para mí, es una cuestión de derechos humanos. Todos los niños tienen derecho a practicar deporte", declaró días antes. Natalie Nakase, preguntada por las declaraciones de Cheryl Reeve, apuntó que "en el mundo y en el deporte, ahora mismo hay demasiado odio". "Recomiendo encarecidamente que la gente siga actuando desde el amor. A mí me encanta actuar desde el amor. Creo que no se ha expresado lo suficiente la palabra amor. Quiero seguir compartiendo eso y también seguir apoyando, porque sé que cuando nos brindamos amor mutuo, sacamos lo mejor de cada uno", declaró. Natalie Nakase cree que "el deporte trata sobre el sentido de pertenencia. Trata sobre la inclusión. Se trata de permitir que cada persona sea auténtica. Defiendo firmemente que las mujeres y las niñas merecen jugar, y eso incluye a las mujeres trans. Así que apuesto totalmente por la inclusión". La mediática Sophie Cunningham, jugadora de las Indiana Fever de la WNBA, reafirmó los comentarios que hizo en un artículo publicado recientemente por ESPN, afirmando que es "cuestión de sentido común" impedir que las deportistas transgénero compitan en deportes femeninos. En el artículo Cunningham expresó su deseo de "proteger a las niñas en los vestuarios" y señaló que "no deberían tener que enfrentarse a hombres biológicos". "Estoy aquí para apoyar a las mujeres biológicas, y creo que hay derechos que deben protegerse. Y, como dije, me mantendré firme en eso. Nunca flaquearé en mis convicciones al respecto. Pero jamás he dicho que odie a la comunidad trans", apuntó Cunningham.

articles.title: Izan Almansa deja el Madrid rumbo a la NCAA
articles.standfirst: El ala-pívot murciano, que había vuelto a la ACB el pasado verano, jugará en Gonzaga donde ya tuvo una fantástica experiencia Saint Supery, hoy en el Valencia Básket
articles.summary: El ala-pívot murciano, que había vuelto a la ACB el pasado verano, jugará en Gonzaga donde ya tuvo una fantástica experiencia Saint Supery, hoy en el Valencia Básket
articles.body: Izan Almansa, ala-pívot internacional de 21 años, había intentando reengancharse al baloncesto europeo de la mano del Real Madrid. Firmó en verano de 2025 después de jugar en el proyecto de formación estadounidense llamado Overtime Elite, en la G-League y también en Australia. Tampoco se ha asentado de blanco, quizá falto de más oportunidades en un equipo donde la exigencia era máxima. Ahora quiere relanzar su carrera en América y, como se sabía desde hace meses, seguirá jugando en la NCAA, en Gonzaga. Así lo ha comunicado el club blanco. "El Real Madrid C. F. e Izan Almansa han acordado dar por finalizada su etapa como jugador de nuestro club. El Real Madrid quiere agradecer a Izan Almansa su compromiso y dedicación durante la temporada en la que ha defendido nuestra camiseta y le desea lo mejor a él y a su familia en esta nueva etapa de su vida.".  Tras rechazar la opción de ir cedido a un club de la Liga Endesa, Izan parte en busca de un buen posicionamiento para alcanzar la NBA y después de firmar un contrato notable (porque la NCAA ya compite en lo económico con los mejores clubes europeos). El ala-pívot murciano, uno de los grandes proyectos del baloncesto español (MVP del Mundial sub 17 2022, MVP del EuroBásket sub18 2022 y MVP del Mundial sub19 2023), jugará con los Bulldogs, donde militó la temporada pasada el base Mario Saint-Supery, que ha fichado por el Valencia Básket. La pasada temporada, Almansa, que creció en la cantera del Madrid, tuvo una presencia testimonial para Sergio Scariolo en lo importante (la Euroliga), con apenas tres partidos disputados. Pese a la falta de pívots y la lesión grave de Garuba en semifinales, Izan no disputó ni un minuto en la Final Four. Eso terminó de convencer de que era mejor salir, algo que terminó de concretar (su destino) en junio. En la Liga Endesa, mientras, si compitió en 19 partidos  (5,1 puntos y 2,3 rebotes de media). ¿Cuál será su siguiente paso?

articles.title: Predicting Every NBA Team's Best Player 3 Years From Now
articles.summary: The New York Knicks were the eighth different NBA champion in eight years, a good illustration of how extreme parity is only making it harder to guess at what each new season will bring.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks were the eighth different NBA champion in eight years, a good illustration of how extreme parity is only making it harder to guess at what each new season will bring.

At least if team performance is becoming impossible to project, the player side is a little more consistent.

That's the hope, anyway, as we look a full three years ahead to the dawn of the 2029-30 campaign and try to guess who'll be each team's top option.

We're not allowed to guess at who might arrive via the draft, or who a team might trade for or sign. We'll take the current roster and do the best we can based on aging curves, likely development (or slippage) and contract status.

The Atlanta Hawks are a team that has nearly everything but a clear first-option superstar. Onyeka Okongwu and Nickeil Alexander-Walker provide spacing and versatile defense at below-market prices, the books are very clean and rookie Kingston Flemings offers youthful upside.

Jalen Johnson still feels like more of a No. 2 on a dangerous team, but he's the man for now and has to be the pick in the absence of anyone with his level of proven production and growth potential. The best thing about the 24-year-old is the five-year, $150 million deal that'll keep him underpaid through 2029-30. With no one on the roster currently making more than that, there's room to add someone above him in the pecking order.

That said, Johnson made the All-NBA Third Team and averaged 22.5 points, 10.3 rebounds and 7.9 assists last year.

So the second-best thing about him is that there's a non-zero chance he becomes a true superstar while still only making $30 million per season.

Though he'll be in his 30s by then, Jayson Tatum still pretty clearly projects to be the Boston Celtics' best player in three years. If it's not him, it'll be someone who's not currently on the roster.

That's no knock on guys like Hugo Gonzalez and Jordan Walsh, who should only be in their early primes by 2029, but those two are role players. Other options like Derrick White (32), Paul George (36) and Payton Pritchard (29) aren't at ages where you're expecting upward trajectories.

If Jaylen Brown were still on the team, maybe this would have been a more interesting exercise. Who's to say how Tatum might age in the wake of that 2025 Achilles tear?

Michael Porter Jr. probably has the distinction at the moment, and new addition Julius Randle is the one with multiple All-NBA nods on his resumé, but neither of those vets seem like big enough features in the Brooklyn Nets' long-term plans to be the team's best player in 2029.

Good. That allows us to consider the merits of far less-proven players, chiefly Brooklyn's last two top-10 picks: Egor Dëmin, who went eighth in 2025, and Mikel Brown Jr., the No. 6 pick in the most recent draft.

Brown is too much of a mystery to make him a responsible pick, while Dëmin shot 38.5 percent from deep last season and showed all the connective passing Brooklyn hoped for. A Summer League performance that saw Dëmin flash rapidly developing on-ball skills and scoring chops inside the arc puts him over the top.

The Nets have loads of young candidates who might only be a breakout away from changing this prediction. Ben Saraf, Nolan Traoré and Noah Clowney have all had their moments, and Clowney is the oldest of the group at just 22.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

The Charlotte Hornets only have two realistic candidates, but Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller both have so much promise that this is the toughest toss-up we've encountered so far.

Knueppel is coming off the best shooting season we've ever seen from a rookie and is three years younger than Miller. What's more, the plus-2.8 Box Plus/Minus Knueppel produced last year as a rookie (while averaging 18.5 points on a 63.3 true shooting percentage) was significantly better than anything Miller managed in any of his first three seasons.

It's still tough to downplay Miller's upside as a potential two-way superstar wing. He has the rangy frame, high-wire athleticism and self-sufficient scoring craft teams covet, along with the physical profile of a three-level scorer who, with some development, might be able to guard the opponent's top wing threat.

Knueppel's floor is exceptionally high, but it's hard to argue he has a ceiling like Miller's.

We're going with the riskier option and choosing Miller. The takeaway here should be that Charlotte has two great cracks at a cornerstone.

Caleb Wilson is a bold choice here, considering he hasn't played a minute of NBA action yet. Josh Giddey is a much more established stat-stuffer, and Matas Buzelis is sitting right there with two seasons of experience at age 21. He's coming off a very strong second campaign marked by averages of 16.3 points and 5.8 boards along with intriguing development as a three-point threat.

Wilson, though, has the high-end draft pedigree as the No. 4 pick in a loaded lottery. It also helps that he used Summer League to flash completely unexpected jump-shooting prowess to go with his top-one-percent athleticism at the forward spot.

Buzelis is far from a slouch in the open floor, but Wilson might be a game-changer. We're speculating pretty hard here, but plenty of early signs are emerging that Wilson is going to have some real offensive skills to pair with a high-revving motor and elite finishing.

The Cleveland Cavaliers need Evan Mobley to be their best player right now , so he'd better be their top talent three seasons into the future.

Mobley disappointed last year relative to expectations. Ahead of 2025-26, most believed he'd build on a brilliant 2024-25 that saw him nearly triple his three-point attempt rate while posting a career-best 37.3 percent accuracy mark. Burying the lede, the 6'11" big man also won Defensive Player of the Year in 2024-25 and made his first All-NBA team.

Put together a season like that, and people are going to be a little bummed when you only follow it up with similar per-game averages on reduced efficiency. The thought was that Mobley was leaving Earth's orbit as a superstar. Instead, he leveled off.

Ahead of his age-25 season, Mobley is still among the top two-way frontcourt players in the sport. He's entering his prime, has already been officially recognized as one of the NBA's premier defenders and is a good bet to continue the offensive growth he's flashed in the past.

Barring a return to form from likely Hall-of-Famer Kyrie Irving, Cooper Flagg is going to be the Dallas Mavericks' best player in 2026-27.

Those who are particularly high on Flagg after a rookie season that included more offensive competency than anticipated might believe he'll be Dallas' top talent regardless of what Irving does.

Flagg's capability as a distributor and scorer were surprises, even if the extra workload produced a worse defensive performance than expected.

Assuming he continues his growth trajectory as a first-option on offense while coming closer to the All-Defense status many took as a given, Flagg should be one of the 10 best two-way players in the league within the time horizon we're considering.

Unless Dallas somehow adds a player with even greater potential, Flagg is one of the easiest choices of this entire exercise.

Nikola Jokić will play his age-34 season in 2029-30, putting him outside his prime but still making him highly likely to be an All-NBA force. Maybe if you're convinced that his relatively limited athleticism means he doesn't have a half-step to lose, Jokić could suffer a steep decline.

More likely, his unsurpassed processing speed, passing eye and scoring touch will allow him to remain the top offensive option in the league deep into his 30s.

The only potential hiccup here is trusting Jokić will be a member of the Denver Nuggets three years from now. There were financial reasons for him to turn down extensions both last offseason and this past summer; he can get larger annual salaries and longer deals by waiting. There are certainly no signals the three-time MVP wants to play anywhere else.

That said, Denver has cut salary via trades and had trouble surrounding Jokić with the level of talent he deserves for several seasons since the 2022-23 title. It wouldn't be a shock if he determined the Nuggets don't give him the best chance to win another championship.

As it stands, Jokić can hit unrestricted free agency in the summer of 2027.

The question isn't whether Cade Cunningham will be the Detroit Pistons' top player three years from now. It's how big the gap will be between him and his team's second option.

Cunningham is only just now entering his prime after proving himself as a legitimate MVP candidate and postseason-minted superstar in 2025-26. He'll hold that level or improve on it through 2029.

Detroit is currently squeezing Jalen Duren in restricted free agency because he, unlike Cunningham, failed to maintain his value in the playoffs. Ausar Thompson is eligible for an extension, but his shooting and playmaking limitations are major hindrances to the Pistons' roster-building effort. If he can't get substantially better on offense, he'll take himself out of the running for Detroit's No. 2 spot behind Cunningham and might even wind up out of the team's plans entirely.

We're only copping out like this once because the Golden State Warriors are on a timeline that screams they'll be a completely different organization before three years have elapsed.

Odds are, Stephen Curry, Draymond Green and Steve Kerr will have retired by the start of the 2029-30 season. The franchise will have either pivoted to a full rebuild or, more likely, lured an in-prime star in free agency. Maybe they'll have done both by then. Life cycles around the league are only accelerating, so anything's possible.

The only certainty here is that nobody on the current roster appears to be a cornerstone capable of holding up through three more seasons. Whoever takes the mantle from Steph isn't on the team yet.

Alperen Sengün is only five months older than Amen Thompson and already has a 2-0 lead in career All-Star games. You'd have to possess a very strong belief in Thompson's ability to grow as a shooter to choose him over his more accomplished teammate.

Defensively, Thompson is at a level Sengün is unlikely to reach. But for Thompson to become Houston's best player, he will need to improve substantially on the 21.9 percent he shot from three-point range. Elite wings generally need at least a credible perimeter shot, and his shooting currently presents a major obstacle to that outcome.

Reed Sheppard should get a smidgen of consideration here, but he needs to prove he's a full-time starter before we project him as the Houston Rockets' alpha by 2029. Last year's 13.5 points per game, 39.4 percent shooting from deep and sixth-place finish in Sixth Man of the Year voting were a good start, but the No. 3 pick from the 2024 draft has a ways to go.

Pascal Siakam is probably a year too old to make him a safe fallback choice for those too concerned about Tyrese Haliburton's health to make him the selection for the Indiana Pacers.

Three years from now, Siakam will be entering his age-35 season. He's held up well so far and was an All-Star in each of the last two years, but the aging curve comes for everyone eventually.

Haliburton is only 26, six years younger than Siakam. Considering the heights he reached before tearing his Achilles, it feels safe to assume he'll still be in his prime (and that his prime will resemble the last few seasons) by 2029.

Lest we forget, Haliburton led Indy to within a win of a championship, already has an assist crown to go with his two All-NBA nods and is on the very shortest list of the league's most singularly transformative offensive forces.

He'll still be a superstar three years from now.

We're getting bold here by going with LA Clippers' recent lottery pick Keaton Wagler over two-time All-Star Darius Garland.

After coming aboard in the James Harden trade last year, Garland looked like the same guy who played a major role on some excellent Cavs teams. In 19 games with the Clips, he put up 19.9 points and 6.4 assists on a 47.1/43.8/86.0 shooting split. Entering his age-27 season, he could make this prediction look bad by simply holding onto that level of production.

Garland is set to earn $44.9 million in 2027-28 before his contract expires. Do the Clippers intend to extend him for what seems certain to be at least $50 million per year when they just drafted someone who plays his same position?

Wagler will only be 22 and still on his rookie-scale deal in three seasons. He could either surpass Garland in effectiveness or simply be the better value by then.

Luka Dončić's current contract is set to expire after 2028-29 if he plays it out all the way through his player option that season. Technically, he's not guaranteed to be on the Los Angeles Lakers in three years.

Dončić didn't choose to join the Lakers and has never really had control over his destination. It's possible he'll want to test free agency.

More likely: Dončić will decline his player option and sign a five-year deal worth over $400 million in the summer of 2028. Assuming that outcome, he'll be one of the half-dozen best players in the league as he enters the later stages of his prime—more than qualifying him for "best player on the team" status.

The bar Dončić set early in his career by making five straight All-NBA First Teams from his age-20 to age-24 seasons will be difficult to clear, but he could regress from that level and still be Los Angeles' obvious top threat.

If he makes good on the statistical profile that suggested he should have been the top draftee in his class, Cam Boozer might be the Memphis Grizzlies' best player when he debuts in October. Three years from now, the gap between him and Memphis' No. 2 option may only be wider.

Boozer has limitations. He doesn't have the run-and-jump burst many teams prioritize in their forwards. In college and during a brief Summer League showing, he did what his believers expected by compensating for those shortcomings with uncommon feel, passing acumen, ball-handling and shooting potential.

What Boozer lacks in speed and bounce, he can make up for with cleverness, power and skill.

To justify the price they paid, the Miami Heat had better hope Giannis Antetokounmpo is still their best player in three years.

If he's not—either because he left after choosing not to extend his contract or because his skills and health declined substantially—the Heat will be in a brutal spot. Though Antetokounmpo's desire to land in Miami may have slightly diminished the trade package headed back to the Milwaukee Bucks, his onboarding came at the cost of an entire lineup's worth of useful players and four first-round assets.

If this roster build doesn't work, the Heat don't have many good outs. Though they could trade Bam Adebayo or Giannis (at reduced value in the hypothetical where he's no longer a superstar), a move like that might not even put them back to neutral from a rebuilding perspective.

The recent set of 2026 draftees, AJ Green and Gary Trent Jr. (for now), are the only players ticketed to collect salaries from the Bucks in 2029-30. That makes No. 10 pick Brayden Burries the easy choice.

Burries' eye-opening Summer League work is doing all the lifting here, but it's hard not to be encouraged by a guy who came into the draft cycle billed as a good defender who could shoot, only to watch him show unexpected on-ball utility. As the Bucks start over, he's the highest-upside piece they have.

Ryan Rollins is a better guard right now and is only heading into his age-25 season. Because his current deal is too team-friendly to make an extension realistic, he's almost assured of hitting unrestricted free agency after the upcoming season. Betting on him to stay in Milwaukee is a risk.

In good news for the Bucks, they also have Kasparas Jakucionis and Kel'el Ware in the up-and-coming category. The former will be a restricted free agent after 2028-29 and could develop into a high-end starter by then.

Here's hoping this pick eases the minds of Minnesota Timberwolves fans who don't love the barely audible whispers that Anthony Edwards is the latest big star other teams are starting to circle.

The Wolves aren't quite all-in on this core after trading assets for LaMelo Ball, but they're running out of ways to change course if this build doesn't work. We've seen this movie before, and it often ends with the incumbent star moving on after several years of banging into a sub-Finals ceiling.

Edwards is fresh off his fourth straight All-Star campaign and has improved his scoring average and true shooting percentage in every season of his career. He could level off right where he's at and pile up top-10 MVP finishes through our three-year time cutoff.

That said, only entering his age-25 season, Edwards should be expected to keep improving.

Nobody Minnesota adds will be a better player than Edwards. Whether or not he's still on the team is the only question.

Choosing Derik Queen here is a bet that the knack he showed for creative and relatively efficient scoring in college will return as he gets further into his pro career. It'll have to.

Queen is undersized at 6'9" for the center spot and doesn't seem likely to excel as a back-line option. That means his craft, passing and foul-drawing will need to improve as he works to turn himself into a power forward through whom the offense runs.

Last year's 79.5 free-throw percentage is a hopeful sign Queen might someday feature a three-point shot worth honoring, and he'll have to be a threat from deep to make any of this work.

Jeremiah Fears has the athletic burst to warrant consideration, and if Trey Murphy III is still on the team in three years, he's easily the safest choice.

The New York Knicks are a veteran team with no projectable youth, unless you think Mohamed Diawara is in for a leap or two. The unlikelihood of a 20-something reaching stardom makes Jalen Brunson the clear choice from among the championship-winning core.

An All-NBA honoree three years running and coming off a no-brainer Finals MVP, Brunson will play his age-30 season in 2026-27. Given his craft and shooting ability, he should age well for a small guard. Decline can come early for that player type, but Brunson isn't dependent on a lightning-quick first step or the ability to rise over larger defenders at the rim. His pivot game, deft touch and herky-jerky style will still be flummoxing defenders as he heads into post-prime territory.

Natural wear and tear will probably mean Brunson is no longer in the MVP conversation by 2029, but he should still be a clear All-Star.

Oklahoma City Thunder: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander

The gap between Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Oklahoma City Thunder's other options—principally Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren—is wide enough today to price in growth for the youngsters and still go with the two-time MVP.

Williams is a tremendous two-way force when healthy, but he's not all that far removed from real questions about his fitness as a first option during OKC's non-SGA minutes. It feels safe to assume that Gilgeous-Alexander, who'll be starting his age-31 season in 2029, will remain an MVP candidate and still be arguably the best offensive weapon in the league.

Holmgren is like Williams in that he's going to make several more All-NBA appearances but almost certainly never reach the MVP tier of difference-makers that SGA has belonged to since 2022-23.

The only real question here is how many more of those trophies Gilgeous-Alexander will collect over the next three seasons. Let's put the over-under at 1.5.

The pendulum has swung pretty far toward the negative on Paolo Banchero, whose production slipped last year in a second-straight non-award-worthy season.

After winning Rookie of the Year and making the All-Star team in his sophomore follow-up, Banchero has battled declining efficiency and faced questions about his fitness as an alpha offensive weapon.

All this just as his supermax extension kicks in.

Maybe Banchero's star has dimmed, but he's only 23 and is still quite clearly the Orlando Magic's highest-ceiling player.

He's a foul-drawing machine whose combination of strength and skill should only make him harder to guard without hacking as he gains experience. And at 31.7 percent from deep for his career, he's not a hopeless case from long range.

Assuming these last two relatively tough seasons encourage Banchero to move the ball more freely and cut the junk food from his shot diet, he should be the Magic's top talent in 2029, when he'll be entering his age-27 season.

VJ Edgecombe's standout rookie season and clear fitness for playoff competition give some pause here, but we can't overthink things in the wake of Tyrese Maxey piling up 28.3 points per game and making an All-NBA team last season.

Skeptics might note that Maxey, 25, might be a candidate for early slippage when his blinding speed starts to go. Given his heavy minute totals (he led the league at 38.0 per game last year), the loss of his peak athleticism is a concern. Fortunately for Maxey, he's a high-volume three-point shooter who sits at 37.7 percent for his career and has been much better than that when not tasked with taking so many tough ones.

Perhaps just as importantly, Maxey has tremendous touch on his floater and doesn't need to get all the way to the basket to remain a serious paint-scoring threat.

Edgecombe could make an All-Star game by 2029, and maybe Jaylen Brown will still be hanging on as a star by then. But Maxey is pretty clearly the pick for Philly.

In an ideal world, the 2029 version of Khaman Maluach would be a dominant defensive center who also spreads the floor as a long-range shooter. When players with his immense size and work ethic pick up the game at 14, it feels slightly less irresponsible to make such wild projections.

Maluach is a very long way from meeting those optimistic forecasts. Devin Booker, meanwhile, is an established star who seems interested in finishing his career with the Phoenix Suns.

Booker will almost assuredly be overpaid on a $69 million salary for 2029-30, his age-33 season. But he's such a polished and professional scorer that he should retain plenty of effectiveness between now and then.

One other factor in Booker's favor: Phoenix is among the teams most bereft of future picks that might bring in a young, high-upside star. It's hard to imagine the Suns adding someone through the draft who'll overtake Booker as he declines.

Deni Avdija came into the league and established himself primarily as a defensive forward who could chip in just enough offense as long as you didn't ask him to shoot too much. Flash forward and he's now one of the best downhill attackers and offensive self-starters in the league.

If you think a guy who could transform himself like that is done growing at 26, you've got another thing coming.

Though new Portland Trail Blazers owner Tom Dundon is pinching pennies all over the place, he seems willing to spend on the roster. He'll have to if he wants to keep Avdija around when his dirt-cheap contract expires after 2027-28, when he'll earn a laughably low $11.9 million.

Scoot Henderson could still pop, and Donovan Clingan will become more interesting if he continues his development as a spacer. But if Avdija comes back on a new deal, he'll still be the man in Portland.

Say it with me, Sacramento Kings, so that we may speak it into existence and avert another several seasons of irrelevance: Darius Acuff Jr. will not be a bust.

Feel free to repeat that as many times as it takes to manifest an outcome Sacramento hopes for but is far from guaranteed to see.

Acuff has work to do if he's going to make a positive impact on winning. The rookie's small frame and inefficient showing in Summer League did not quiet concerns about his future. But if not him, who even profiles as a realistic option on the Kings roster?

Keegan Murray, who's somehow declining in his mid-20s? Domantas Sabonis, who's already on the wrong side of 30? Nique Clifford?

So let's spend a few paragraphs making the case for Harrison Barnes. See, the thing you're really not considering about locker-room sages is...

OK, we all know there's no point in choosing anyone but Victor Wembanyama. That was just an attempt to make this mildly interesting. A better and much more realistic head-fake would have involved talking up Dylan Harper as an alternative based on Wemby's occasionally concerning health issues and Harper's pretty clear future as an All-NBA force.

Even that would be too disingenuous to maintain for more than a sentence or two.

Wemby is the reigning Defensive Player of the year and should win that award every season for the next decade or so while adding layers upon layers to his offensive game. If he doesn't have an MVP or two by 2029, it'll be a surprise.

Scottie Barnes would have to endure a bizarre slide as he enters what should be his prime, and one of the Toronto Raptors' intriguing youngsters would need to develop far beyond role-player status to make this pick interesting.

Considering Barnes is coming off his most complete regular season and a stunningly good playoff performance (24.1 points, 8.6 assists, 6.1 rebounds), he doesn't seem like a candidate for slippage. And while Collin Murray-Boyles and rookie Allen Graves are going to figure prominently in Toronto's success going forward, those two don't come with obvious star upside.

Barnes has already made a couple of All-Star games, finished fifth in DPOY voting last year and may now be moving into a phase where he can be his team's offensive engine in a postseason setting. At 25, he's also not done improving.

The Utah Jazz have two immensely promising younger options in rookie Darryn Peterson and second-year wing Ace Bailey. Either could become stars in three years.

Complicating matters, they also have two much more established in-prime options in Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr.

It's tempting to go with JJJ here. He's got three All-Defensive nods, a DPOY award and multiple seasons shooting at least 37.0 percent from long range. He's making an average of $51 million through 2029-30 for a reason.

We still haven't discussed Keyonte George, though, and he falls somewhere between Utah's speculative prospects and the more established Jackson.

In his age-22 season, George exploded. He put up 23.6 points per game, hit 37.1 percent from deep on good volume and compromised defenders often enough to shoot 7.1 free throws per game, making 89.2 percent of them. He might be a bigger, more aggressive, craftier Darius Garland, which is basically a perennial All-NBA candidate if he can stay healthy.

The risk with George is that his breakout came in 54 mostly meaningless games last year. It's impossible to be sure what he did was real, but we're going with him anyway.

Unless it's an unusually weak class (hey there, 2024!), the team that selects first should be deeply disappointed if the guy they pick doesn't wind up atop their depth chart in three years' time.

The Washington Wizards don't have to worry about that. AJ Dybantsa is going to be a star.

Maybe he'll have some flaws if his long-range shot doesn't develop as hoped, but huge, athletic wings who know how to win one-on-one matchups and have every defensive tool a team could want don't tend to flop.

Dybantsa has obstacles in vets like Trae Young and Anthony Davis, and the former is locked into a deal that'll keep him on the team through 2029 barring a trade. The Wizards are also stocked with other prospects like Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George and Tre Johnson who could all theoretically ascend.

In the end, Dybantsa is a No. 1 pick in a strong draft class who is supposed to take over this team sooner than later. He will.

Stats courtesy of NBA.com , Basketball Reference and Cleaning the Glass . Salary info via Spotrac .

Grant Hughes covers the NBA for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, where he appears with Bleacher Report's Dan Favale .

articles.title: New Video Drops of LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey's 1st Workout as 76ers Teammates
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers' newest stars have begun to build their on-court rapport.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers' newest stars have begun to build their on-court rapport.

LeBron James, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey recently worked out together with trainer Chris Johnson, offering fans a taste of what's to come.

The Sixers tip off the 2026-27 season on Oct. 20 against the New York Knicks. Training camp, which opens Sept. 29, doesn't allow a lot of time for the new-look roster to coalesce before that.

In addition to James and Brown, Philly added Anfernee Simons, Dean Wade, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Labaron Philon Jr. That's a lot of turnover for one offseason.

Having some players hit the gym for informal sessions will undoubtedly ease the transition a bit.

articles.title: Olivia Miles Suffers Ankle Injury, Latest Updates on Lynx Star After Win vs. Valkyries
articles.summary: An ankle injury to Olivia Miles dampened some of the enthusiasm after the Minnesota Lynx rookie delivered another strong performance in Wednesday's 77-66 win over the Golden State Valkyries.
articles.body:
An ankle injury to Olivia Miles dampened some of the enthusiasm after the Minnesota Lynx rookie delivered another strong performance in Wednesday's 77-66 win over the Golden State Valkyries.

Miles finished with 20 points, five, rebounds, seven assists, two steals and two blocks in 30 minutes of action. She exited in the fourth quarter after stepping on the foot of teammate Napheesa Collier.

"I don't have any idea where it's at," Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve told reporters regarding the severity of the ankle injury. "Obviously we're hoping she's OK."

Miles is the runaway favorite for Rookie of the Year. Through 35 games, she's averaging 19.5 points and 6.1 assists. She's also shooting 50.3 percent from the floor and 40.7 percent from beyond the arc.

The 5'10" playmaker is the biggest reason the Lynx have the league's best record (30-7) despite Collier being sidelined until mid-July. She has displayed a level of poise belying her rookie status.

Needless to say, Miles is a critical piece in Minnesota's quest to win a WNBA title. Collier hasn't missed a beat since returning to the court, but the on/off splits tell the story. The Lynx have been 7.9 points per possession worse with Miles on the bench, per WNBA.com .

The team is back in action Friday against the Washington Mystics and then hosts the Valkyries on Monday. Minnesota is afforded an even longer break before its next contest (Aug. 30 against the Atlanta Dream).

If Miles' injury is serious enough to take her out of the lineup, maybe she won't have to miss many games.

articles.title: New Knicks Rumors on Josh Hart's Projected Contract After Becoming Eligible for $132M Deal
articles.summary: The New York Knicks have veteran wing Josh Hart under team control through the 2027-28 NBA season, but it might not be too early to begin serious negotiations over an extension.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks have veteran wing Josh Hart under team control through the 2027-28 NBA season, but it might not be too early to begin serious negotiations over an extension.

The Athletic's James L. Edwards III reported Thursday reported some around the league see Hart commanding a three-year deal. One source pegged the value between $54 and $62 million, and another suggested $60 million is the low end.

He can sign for up to $132 million over four years right now.

"An extension that pays Hart at least $20 million annually feels like a big win for New York," Edwards wrote. "Yet, if you're Hart and look around the league at what other 'glue guys' are getting paid, there's a strong case to be made that conversations should start in the mid-to-high 20s."

The Knicks insider brought up Boston Celtics guard Derrick White (four years, $118 million) and Phoenix Suns wing Dillon Brooks (three years, $73 million) as comparable examples.

Peyton Watson could be another reference point for Hart's representatives. The forward will earn $88 million over four years from the Cleveland Cavaliers as part of a sign-and-trade, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

It's difficult to imagine Hart leaving the Big Apple. He knows he can compete for titles in New York, and he has such a close friendship with teammate Jalen Brunson.

However, the 31-year-old is probably looking at his last best chance to get a huge contract, and he's bound to have suitors if he wants to test the market. Rival contenders will be eager to pursue a player who has averaged 10.5 points and 7.0 rebounds while shooting 35.0 percent on three-pointers across nine seasons.

"My gut tells me the Knicks and Hart will get an extension done at some point," Edwards concluded in his report. "The two sides are better together than apart, and I think they both know that."

That deduction makes plenty of sense. The Knicks' desire to avoid the second apron of the luxury tax and Hart's personal motivations could prove to be complicating factors.

articles.title: The Denver Nuggets Are Failing Nikola Jokić
articles.summary: August is often a quiet stretch of the NBA's calendar, but the volume ratcheted way up Wednesday when ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the Denver Nuggets were trading one of Nikola Jokić's most intriguing young teammates, Peyton Watson, to the Cleveland Cavaliers in a five-team deal.
articles.body:
August is often a quiet stretch of the NBA's calendar, but the volume ratcheted way up Wednesday when ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the Denver Nuggets were trading one of Nikola Jokić's most intriguing young teammates, Peyton Watson, to the Cleveland Cavaliers in a five-team deal.

In a vacuum, the move is maybe justifiable.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

Watson has a career average of 8.7 points and a 36.1 three-point percentage. Without the one truly high-level stretch of his NBA career (January of this year), those numbers are even worse .

With little more than that context to rely on, Denver's unwillingness to pay him $22 million per year and plunge itself that much further past the second apron might seem fair. (The Nuggets were already above the second apron even without Watson.)

The problem is that there's more context. A lot more.

Chief among the reasons why this deal has been widely pilloried is what it appears to say about the organization's commitment to Jokić.

He isn't just the best player in franchise history. Statistically, he's one of the best players in NBA history .

Jokić is first all-time in career player efficiency rating , box plus/minus and win shares per 48 minutes (catch-all metrics that endeavor to quantify a player's impact in a single number). He's tied for first all-time in career triple-doubles (including the playoffs). He's one of just 10 players in league history with three MVPs. And he's sixth all-time in career MVP shares, behind only LeBron James, Michael Jordan, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Larry Bird and Magic Johnson.

Despite all of the accolades he's already piled up, Jokić is smack-dab in the middle of his prime. The 31-year-old has a mostly ground-bound game that should age relatively well. And his team basically just punted on the restricted free agency of its biggest and perhaps best upside bet.

Moving Watson for a first-round pick that won't convey until Jokić is 36 years old—with no players along with it, young or otherwise—all but seals this summer being a fourth straight loser since the Nuggets won the championship in 2023.

In the offseason immediately after the title run, Denver lost Bruce Brown (although CBA rules made that one inevitable). The next summer, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope walked. In 2025, they traded Michael Porter Jr. and draft capital for Cameron Johnson and lost Russell Westbrook. Along the way, they signed Dario Šarić, Jonas Valančiūnas, both of whom are gone.

This summer, they lost Watson and Tim Hardaway Jr. For most of that stretch, Zeke Nnaji's inexplicable four-year extension (which comes with a $7.5 million player option in 2027-28) has been on the books. And at one point, the front office attached three second-round picks to salary dump Reggie Jackson.

Individually, up until the Watson move—and with the exception of a handful of others, like Nnaji and Jackson—there were reasonable explanations. The Porter-for-Johnson swap, in particular, added flexibility without losing shooting. However, MPJ quickly showed how much higher the Nuggets' ceiling might've been with him when he averaged 25.6 points, 3.8 threes and 3.2 assists while shooting 39.8 percent from deep in his first 38 games with the Brooklyn Nets.

Even some of the moves that could be justified at the time, like the Porter deal or Christian Braun's extension, are off to rough starts. When you look at everything over the last four offseasons together, it feels disastrous.

Jokić is the kind of talent whose presence on a roster guarantees competitiveness, but winning at the highest level requires more than that. It certainly requires more than tactically retreating year after year.

If the basketball world at large perceives Denver's post-championship approach as that, it's not hard to imagine Jokić starting to see it the same.

For years, whenever the subject comes up, Jokić has insisted that he wants to stick with the Nuggets for his entire career. He opted not to sign an extension this summer because he can sign for more (five years and more than $350 million) next summer, but nothing's guaranteed.

This roster is better than the general reaction it's gotten this summer. Jamal Murray is in his prime and played at an All-NBA level last season. Aaron Gordon is among the best and most versatile third options in the league. For long stretches of last season, Johnson looked like the ideal gap-filler for this roster.

If Braun is healthier, he could bounce back to around the level that earned him his big payday. Marvin Bagley III was an underrated pickup this summer. And though he wouldn't come with the same upside as Watson, the rumored acquisition of DeMar DeRozan would uplift the bench.

The group could certainly outperform expectations, get back into the hunt for championships and give Jokić plenty of confidence to sign a massive contract next summer. But again, nothing is guaranteed.

Gordon's health has been a massive question mark since the Nuggets' title run. Johnson shot the ball well last season and is more consistent defensively than MPJ, but his offensive highs may not be as high. Braun may have just caught lightning in a bottle the season before signing his extension. And the non-Jokić minutes have been a wild ride for most of his MVP era.

With the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs younger and more athletic than Denver, the Nuggets' kryptonite Minnesota Timberwolves adding LaMelo Ball and fewer teams blatantly tanking, Jokić could be in for another early playoff exit this coming season.

If that happens on the heels of these last four offseasons, especially if Watson's breakout continues for the Cavaliers, it would be hard to blame Jokić's eye for wandering toward other teams.

articles.title: Matas Buzelis Says Luka Doncic Dropped 'Nasty' Trash Talk During Bulls vs. Lakers Matchup
articles.summary: Luka Dončić is one of the best players in the NBA. He is also one of the league's best trash-talkers.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić is one of the best players in the NBA. He is also one of the league's best trash-talkers.

During an appearance on Cousins with Vince Carter & Tracy McGrady (53-minute mark), the Chicago Bulls forward recalled a time when Dončić was saying things he couldn't even repeat all while dropping 51 points in a Los Angeles Lakers victory.

"I don't really want to get into detail because it was some really like nasty things said, but he just started he started baking me bad, like 12 in a row, bad, and I was like I don't care, keep doing that, I don't care what you doing, keep scoring, we'll see if you can keep scoring," Buzelis said. "I have 20 at half and he has 22. So I'm chilling.

"So I end with like 23. ... And he ends with like 50. And it's just man, he hit this one shot. ... And I'm not even trying to glaze or anything, but he shot it. … He was isoing, and he does that step back, shot it. I feel like in midair he like points directly down at me, and I'm in the corner, and he like turns around mid shot and it just went straight back rim. I was like, 'Oh god, that's not good.' They beat us by like 20. In the media I was saying that I'm probably not going to trash talk again to him, but I really don't care. I'm going to do it again."

While Buzelis deserves some credit for not backing down when it comes to the trash-talk department, there is something to be said about not poking the bear when it comes to some players in the NBA.

And Dončić is certainly one of those players.

The specific game Buzelis referenced was Los Angeles' 142-130 victory over the Bulls on March 12. Dončić ended up with 51 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists on 17-of-31 shooting from the field and a head-turning 9-of-14 shooting from deep.

Austin Reaves also ended up with 30 points, but he, along with everyone else, was an afterthought to Dončić's individual brilliance.

It was yet another reminder of how unstoppable the future Hall of Famer can be when he gets rolling, and he surely let Buzelis and everyone else on the Bulls know about it as he was dropping 51 points.

articles.title: UNC to Face Kentucky, Arkansas, Indiana on Non-Conference Schedule for Michael Malone's 1st Season
articles.summary: Heading into Michael Malone's first season as head coach, North Carolina has finalized its non-conference schedule for the 2026-27 campaign.
articles.body:
Heading into Michael Malone's first season as head coach, North Carolina has finalized its non-conference schedule for the 2026-27 campaign.

The Tar Heels dropped their 17-game out-of-conference games on Thursday, including marquee matchups against Indiana on Oct. 18, Arkansas on Dec. 1 and Kentucky on Dec. 19.

Six of the games will be played at neutral-site locations. Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis will play host to the matchup with the Hoosiers. The game will also be a preseason exhibition contest.

The Tar Heels will face Kentucky at Madison Square Garden. Other venues they will play in include Spectrum Center in Charlotte (vs. West Virginia), First Horizon Coliseum in Greensboro (vs. NC State) and Bridgestone Arena in Nashville (vs. Illinois).

In addition to its non-conference schedule, North Carolina will play 17 games against ACC competition. Dates and times for those games has not yet been announced.

This season marks the start of a new era in Chapel Hill with Malone taking over as head coach. He is replacing Hubert Davis, who was fired in March after the Tar Heels lost in the first round of the NCAA tournament to VCU.

Davis went 125-54 in five seasons and made the NCAA tournament four times, reaching the Final Four in his first season in 2021-22.

Malone was hired on April 7, marking his first stint as a head coach at the college level. He has experience in college, having spent eight seasons as an assistant at three different universities from 1994 to 2001.

The 54-year-old Malone has 12 seasons of head-coaching experience in the NBA, including a 10-year run with the Denver Nuggets from 2015 to '25. He owns a 510-394 career record and won the 2022-23 NBA championship.

articles.title: El nuevo desafío asiático de Luis Guil: "Si en el Real Madrid no consigues resultados, sabes lo que puede pasar"
articles.standfirst: Luis Guil es el nuevo seleccionador de Jordania
articles.summary: Luis Guil es el nuevo seleccionador de Jordania
articles.body: Luis Guil tiene nuevo destino. Meses después de su salida del Real Madrid, el ex ayudante de Sergio Scariolo en el conjunto blanco y en la selección, dirigirá a la selección de Jordania. Será su segunda aventura asiática tras Japón y tendrá el reto de clasificar al equipo jordano para el Mundial 2027 y crear una estructura de baloncesto en la Federación. Desde Taiwán, en plena preparación de la Ventana de Agosto, atendió la llamada de Radio MARCA. Un proyecto que va mucho más allá de las próximas ventanas de agosto: “No solamente es clasificar al equipo para el Mundial, sino crear una forma, una identidad de juego dentro de la Federación de Jordania”. El objetivo inmediato es ambicioso: Jordania marcha segunda de su grupo, con cinco victorias y una derrota, en una fase en la que se mide a Australia, Nueva Zelanda y Filipinas. Guil reconoce que la propuesta le sedujo especialmente por la posibilidad de trabajar también con las categorías inferiores y construir una estructura común para todo el baloncesto jordano. “La federación me proponía liderar todo el tema de las categorías inferiores junto con la senior, e ir en un mismo camino, un poco parecido a lo que se hizo en la Federación, en la selección española, en los últimos años”, explica. El técnico, con amplia experiencia en las categorías de formación españolas y tras su paso por Japón, considera que Jordania tiene una buena base para crecer y competir de nuevo en un Mundial. Su primer contacto con el nuevo equipo ha sido, además, de máxima exigencia. “Todo ha sido muy rápido”, admite Guil, que pasó apenas 24 horas en Ammán antes de viajar a Taiwán para disputar un torneo internacional. Para preparar las ventanas, el entrenador apuesta por conocer primero a fondo a sus jugadores y adaptar sus ideas a las características de la plantilla. Entre los nombres destacados está Rondae Hollis-Jefferson, además de jugadores con experiencia internacional y universitarios estadounidenses. Guil también se apoyará en su conocimiento de Australia y Filipinas y en los contactos que conserva de su etapa en Asia. La nueva aventura llega después de una temporada en el Real Madrid que terminó sin títulos y con la salida de Scariolo y su cuerpo técnico. Guil no esconde que le habría gustado otro desenlace, pero entiende la decisión: “Pena te da que no consigas los resultados, pero sabes a qué club vas, vas al Real Madrid, con el objetivo de ganarlo todo, absolutamente todo”. Pese a ello, hace un balance muy positivo de su etapa en el conjunto blanco: “Me siento halagado por ser elegido por el Madrid y por Sergio” y destaca especialmente haber disputado una Euroliga de máximo nivel y una Final Four que el equipo tuvo al alcance hasta el último tiro. Y si hay una figura determinante en su carrera, esa es Sergio Scariolo. Guil, que trabajó durante años a su lado en la selección española y volvió a hacerlo en Madrid, lo define como “un referente total” tanto por sus conocimientos técnico-tácticos como por su método de trabajo. “Es una persona que crea formas de trabajo, deja un legado en la forma de trabajar”, asegura. Ahora, ya como primer entrenador de una selección, afronta el desafío de aplicar todo ese aprendizaje a Jordania: intentar alcanzar el Mundial de Qatar 2027 y, al mismo tiempo, construir los cimientos de un proyecto que vaya mucho más allá de una sola competición.

articles.title: Dan Hurley Shares Photos Rewatching UConn's Dramatic March Madness Win vs. Duke on IG
articles.summary: Sports fans constantly relive old games and highlights, especially the dramatic ones that saw their teams prevail.
articles.body:
Sports fans constantly relive old games and highlights, especially the dramatic ones that saw their teams prevail.

It turns out, so does UConn men's basketball coach Dan Hurley.

UConn's 73-72 victory over Duke to clinch a spot in the Final Four was arguably the most dramatic game of the entire NCAA men's tournament last season, and the Huskies head coach relived it and experienced some of the emotions that came with Braylon Mullins' buzzer-beater all over again:

If Hurley is going to watch old highlights and post about them online, there are far worse games to choose than the one he did.

After all, it seemed like the Blue Devils were going to cruise to an Elite Eight victory when they built a 19-point lead in the first half. However, UConn gradually cut into the deficit and gave itself a chance in the final seconds.

With Duke leading by two in those final seconds, the Huskies deflected a Cayden Boozer pass near midcourt. The ball ended up in Mullins' hands, and he launched a shot from well beyond the arc to win it.

"It just felt like the window where you've just got to let March Madness take over," Hurley told reporters at the time. "March magic."

UConn ended up defeating Illinois in the Final Four before losing to Michigan in the national championship game. It was quite the run for a program that also won back-to-back national championships in 2023 and 2024 and has established itself as one of the gold standards in the sport.

Hurley was the head coach for both of those titles as well, but the Duke win has to be among the most memorable of his entire tenure.

So memorable, in fact, that he is reliving the highlights during the offseason.

articles.title: James Harden, Cavs Agree to New Contract After Peyton Watson Trade, Full Details Revealed
articles.summary: Veteran guard James Harden is sticking with the Cleveland Cavaliers for the next three years.
articles.body:
Veteran guard James Harden is sticking with the Cleveland Cavaliers for the next three years.

Harden and the Cavs agreed to a new three-year, $97 million contract on Thursday, agents Mike Silverman, Troy Payne and Brandon Grier of Equity Sports told ESPN's Shams Charania . The deal includes a player option and a trade kicker.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

Harden had previously declined his $42.3 million player option for the 2026-27 season before signing the new deal.

This news comes after Cleveland acquired Peyton Watson from in a three-team deal:

Harden also previously said that a "Big 3" of him, Donovan Mitchell and free-agent forward LeBron James was "the goal." However, James ultimately chose to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers.

The Cavs acquired Harden from the Los Angeles Clippers in exchange for point guard Darius Garland and a second-round draft pick at this season's trade deadline. He helped Cleveland finish fourth in the Eastern Conference with a 52-30 record after averaging 20.5 points, 4.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists in 26 regular-season games with his new team.

During the playoffs, Harden averaged 19.2 points, 5.1 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 1.7 steals as the Cavs went on to get swept by the eventual NBA champion New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference Finals. Harden shot just 29.9 percent from three-point range during the postseason, and his defensive shortcomings were exposed time and time again.

Still, Harden is one of the league's best offensive players, and his presence ensures that Cleveland will remain one of the top contenders in the Eastern Conference. He and Mitchell create a talented backcourt duo, and he's shown that he can help elevate the production from big men Jarrett Allen and Evan Mobley.

With Harden sticking around for the foreseeable future, the Cavs can focus on adding other pieces to improve the roster as they gear up to chase an NBA title next season.

Harden has agreed to a three-year, $97 million contract with the Cleveland Cavaliers, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

That brings Harden's career earnings to a total of $511 million, per Charania .

articles.title: Patrick Soon-Shiong 'Absolutely' Won't Sell Lakers Share to Iger, Kushner Amid Buss Family Dispute
articles.summary: Amid the ongoing Buss family drama tied to the Los Angeles Lakers sale to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner, another one of their minority owners has no plans to sell his stake in the franchise.
articles.body:
Amid the ongoing Buss family drama tied to the Los Angeles Lakers sale to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner, another one of their minority owners has no plans to sell his stake in the franchise.

In a statement to ESPN's Dave McMenamin , the attorney for Dr. Patrick Soon-Shiong said he has "absolutely" no intention of selling his four percent stake in the Lakers:

"Dr. Patrick is absolutely not selling his minority share of the Lakers. Bob Iger and Josh Kushner are good friends, and we will be joining them as supportive, active and engaged partners once they close the transaction with Mr. Walter. We are extremely excited about the Lakers' future and look forward to many more championship years."

ESPN's Ramona Shelburne reported on Aug. 12 that Mark Walter was selling his majority share of the Lakers to Iger and Kushner at a $12.5 billion valuation.

The move came as a surprise because the ink was barely dry on Walter's purchase of the Lakers, which was approved by the NBA board of governors last October.

Things have only gotten more complicated in the time since the Iger-Kushner purchase was reported. In particular, the Buss family is at odds right now over their 17.8 percent stake in the Lakers.

Jeanie Buss, who has been governor of the franchise since 2013, is contesting the vote from her five siblings to sell their stake.

When Walter purchased the franchise last year, the deal included an agreement to keep Jeanie on as governor through at least the 2030 season.

McMenamin noted if the five other Buss siblings sell their stake in the Lakers, Jeanie would retain around a three percent share of the franchise. NBA rules require at least a 15 percent ownership stake to operate as a governor.

The Buss family has owned some portion of the Lakers since 1979 when Dr. Jerry Buss purchased the franchise, along with the Los Angeles Kings and The Forum, for $67.5 million .

Soon-Shiong bought his share of the Lakers in 2010 from Magic Johnson for an undisclosed amount, though estimates at the time suggested Johnson's stake was valued at around $30 million.

Based on the $12.5 billion valuation that Iger and Kushner are paying, Soon-Shiong's stake is worth roughly $500 million.

articles.body: Era uno de los agentes libres más atractivos del mercado aunque nadie esperaba que cambiara de aires. Y no lo hará. James Harden, tras renunciar a su opción de jugador en junio y 42 millones, llegó a un acuerdo con los Cavs para seguir en el equipo las tres próximas temporadas con un contrarto por 97 millones de dólares. La tercera temporada será una opción de jugador. El acuerdo convertirá a 'La Barba' en el cuarto jugador que más dinero haya ganado en la historia de la NBA. De hecho será el cuarto que supere el límite de los 500 millones ganados a lo largo de una carrera (511 para 'La Barba') después de LeBron James, Kevin Durant y Stephen Curry. En pocos días, 26 de agosto, Harden cumplirá los 37 años y podría estender su carrera hasta los 40 si cumple todo el contrato con Cleveland. Es el segundo jugador de la historia que firma un contrato garantizado por más de 90 millones a los 37 años. El otro, claro, fue LeBron. Además, 'La Barba' que inicia su temporada 18 en la NBA, podrá redondear su trayectoria con las 20 temporadas en activo. Harden, en lugar de preferir los 42 millones de su último año, prefirió trabajar con los Cavs en dos escenarios, un contrato de dos años y otro de tres, el último como opción de jugador, que es el que ha prevalecido. Además el tiempo de espera ha permitido a los Cavs trabajar en el resto de su plantilla. La opción elegida permite a los Cavs pagar a Harden en tres años en lugar de dos y así poder transitar por debajo del primer y segundos aprons en el límite salarial. Si 'La Barba' cumple con su trasuectoria, los Cavs no acabarán con récord negativo de victorias en la Liga regular, nunca lo ha hecho Harden en todos los equipos que ha jugado. articles.title: Jokic gana a Wembanyama rozando el triple-doble
articles.standfirst: El serbio se despachó con 20 puntos, nueve rebotes y ocho asistencias ante Francia
articles.summary: El serbio se despachó con 20 puntos, nueve rebotes y ocho asistencias ante Francia
articles.body: Serbia y Francia eligieron jugar un par de amistosos antes de afrontar los dos compromisos de las Ventanas de clasificación para el Mundial de 2027. Y el caso es que eligieron hacerlo uno contra otro, convirtiendo su doble enfrentamiento en la fiesta del baloncesto antes de los partidos oficiales de la FIBA. No está nada mal pasar varias semanas sin competición y retomar la actividad con un duelo entre dos de las mejores selecciones del mundo y dos de los mejores jugadores del planeta. Serbia se llevó el primer duelo, el jugado en Belgrado, este jueves 90-87. Lo ganó en un choque que llegó muy igualado al descanso pero en el que los locales fueron mejores tras la reanudación. Pero lo que el mundo del baloncesto quería ver es a Nikola Jokic y Victor Wembanyama bailando en la pintura, uno contra otro en un duelo en el que ya se puede fantasear de cara al próximo Mundial... si los dos equipos se clasifican. El 'Joker' fue mejor. Las dudas de si iban a jugar mucho o poco incluso de si iban a coincidir se disiparon cuando ambos se midieron en el salto incial del partido. Luego varias acciones como un taponazo del francés cuando el serbio trataba de machacar, un par de mates de 'Wemby', uno de espaldas de los que tanto abusa con los Spurs, o varias lecciones al poste del serbio que puso en juego más arsenal ofensivo que su rival. A estos partidos los llaman amistosos (friendly match), pero de amistosos tienen poco. Sirven para rodar a los equipos , recién acoplados, pero en un partido entre Jokic y Wembanyama, todos los focos apuntan a los dos jugadores interiores más dominantes del mundo. Serbia tuvo que ganar el partido dos veces. Llegó al descanso con una ventaja mínima, 46-45, tras una ligera ventaja francesa, 29-34, mediado el segundo cuarto. En la reanudación el equipo local pareció entrar con mejor pie y empezó a construir una ventaja que pareció definitiva cuando quedaban 5:41 para el final del partido, 82-69. Eran los mejores momentos de Jokic que dominaba el choque con números que se acercaron al triple-doble (para él no hay amistosos, un partido es un partido y acabó con 20 puntos, 9 rebotes y 8 asistencias  y 33 de valoración). También eran momentos de inspiración para Milutinov (15), Avramovic (13) y Dobric (12). Pero Francia no había dicho su última palabra. Un parcial de 0-9 en dos minutos colocó el 86-83 a falta de 1:01 que se apretó mucho más a falta de 11 segundos con el 88-86. Dos tiros libres de Avramovic y otros dos de Dobric colocaron el definitivo 90-87 que cerró el primer gran duelo entre dos colosos. Wembanyama perdió el duelo colectivo y el individual, ofreciendo algunos chispazos pero con una segunda mitad muy floja. Firmó 10 puntos, 5 rebotes  y 2 asistencias para 10 de valoración. El mejor anotador en Francia fue Noua (14), seguido por Francisco (13) y por Gerald Ayayi (10). En materia reboteadora, el propio Ayayi y Noua igualaron los cinco rebotes de 'Wemby'. Ambos equipos continuarán su preparación este domingo (18.00) en la devolución de visita de Serbia, esta vez en suelo francés (en el CO’Met Arena de Orleans). Una nueva ocasión de poder disfrutar de dos de los mejores jugadores de su tiempo.

articles.title: Un test mundial para España
articles.standfirst: La selección juega el torneo internacional de Tenerife ante Nigeria y Bélgica
articles.summary: La selección juega el torneo internacional de Tenerife ante Nigeria y Bélgica
articles.body: En una exigente preparación para el Mundial, la selección femenina de baloncesto debe medirse a cinco equipos que estarán en la cita de Berlín. Ya lo hizo ante Alemania (60-65) en el primer test, un rival al que se volverá a enfrentar ya en el estreno del Mundial (4 de septiembre). Ahora llega el gran torneo internacional de Tenerife, con partidos ante Nigeria y Bélgica, y la gira se cerrará en Zaragoza, ante Mali, otro rival del grupo de España y China, antes de viajar a Alemania. El equipo que dirige Miguel Méndez afronta un excelente torneo en Tenerife que da mucho brillo a la gira ‘Volvemos a soñar’. El Santiago Martín acoge tres grandes partidos empezando este mismo viernes, a las 21.00 horas (tdp), con un España - Nigeria, siguiendo el sábado con el Bélgica - Nigeria y cerrando el torneo el domingo con el España - Bélgica. En liza, las campeonas de África (Nigeria) y Europa (Bélgica) y equipos que, como España, buscarán estar en la lucha por las medallas en Berlín. El partido será muy espceial para dos jugadoras canarias, Elena Buenavida, nacida en Santa Cruz de Tenerife, y Maite Cazorla, en Las Palmas. Las dos jugarán ante su afición en un torneo que la escolta del Valencia Basket analizaba así: “Qué mejor que jugar contra dos rivales como Nigeria y Bélgica que son de lo más top del mundo”. Para ambas será un orgullo este test Mundial para España. Para el partido de este viernes ante Nigeria, al margen de las bajas por tener jugadoras en la WNBA, Méndez tendrá que hacer dos descartes en cada partido en su lista de 14 convocadas. En Nigeria, también sin alguna jugadora todavía en competición en la NBA, las referencias en el partido serán Ezinne Kalu, la líder y directora de juego, Murjanatu Musa, una jugadora muy dominnate en la pintura, y Victoria Macaulau, autora de 13,6 puntos de media en los partidos de clasificación para el Mundial.

Denver Nuggets star Nikola Jokić had high praise for San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama after they faced off in a friendly international matchup on Thursday.
