articles.title: Dillon Brooks Makes Bold Shai Gilgeous-Alexander Claim in New Video, 'I Had His Number'
articles.summary: Phoenix Suns star Dillon Brooks feels his team's first-round sweep by the Oklahoma City Thunder might have been the start of a new rivalry between him and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.
articles.body:
Phoenix Suns star Dillon Brooks feels his team's first-round sweep by the Oklahoma City Thunder might have been the start of a new rivalry between him and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

Brooks said in a Thursday episode of NBA 2K League that he's hoping to take on Gilgeous-Alexander again next season.

"A little rivalry brewing up. I live for those," Brooks said around the 4:40 mark of the podcast. "If we get them again this year, it's definitely going to be Shai.

"Before he got to this level— because he's one of the greatest in the game right now— I had his number."

This isn't the first time Brooks has professed to have the "number" of one of the NBA's top players. He made a similar comment about San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama in February.

"I have his number. Go check that up, and he knows it too," Brooks told streamer N3on in February. "That's the one guy in the NBA that I have his number and everybody is taking that blueprint at guarding him."

Brooks and Gilgeous-Alexander traded jabs during and after the Thunder's first-round sweep of the Thunder this April.

The two Team Canada teammates still shared an embrace after the Thunder's Game 4 and have since competed on the same team as Canada works to qualify for the 2027 FIBA World Cup.

Brooks said on Thursday's podcast appearance his matchups against Gilgeous-Alexander took place when Brooks was playing for the Memphis Grizzlies.

"We can go to the stats," Brooks said on Thursday's podcast. "Memphis... that's when the foul bait wasn't a real thing. Those times I can get away with the get-out-the-way type s--t."

He also said he expected not his longstanding feud with LeBron James but his matchups against Wembanyama to become another rivalry to watch going forward.

"You're going to start seeing that I'm going to get more agitated with him," Brooks said about Wembanyama.

Wembanyama and Brooks never met up last season. Wembanyama put up 23 points in 20 minutes through three games against Brooks the season prior .

Brooks and Gilgeous-Alexander will meet again as regular-season opponents when the Suns travel to Oklahoma City for their first road game of the season this Monday. He will get his first chance to play Wembanyama when the Spurs come to Phoenix Nov. 9.

articles.title: Dillon Brooks Says He 'Loves' Facing LeBron James, Lakers Playoff Game Meme 'Was Not Scripted'
articles.summary: One of the NBA's most notable recent rivalries is the one between LeBron James and Dillon Brooks.
articles.body:
One of the NBA's most notable recent rivalries is the one between LeBron James and Dillon Brooks.

But Brooks said he doesn't consider it a rivalry at this point.

"I love playing against him," Brooks said (5:30 mark). "Honestly, it's not even a rivalry; it's like a competitive spirit because I've watched him my whole life."

Jayson Tatum's dad blunt about Celtics roster

Brooks added that the meme of him sitting courtside at a Los Angeles Lakers game wasn't "scripted."

Brooks and the Phoenix Suns didn't face James in the playoffs this year, but that didn't stop him from getting a courtside seat to the Lakers' loss against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

That was just the latest wrinkle in the back-and-forth between Brooks and James.

The origin of the beef dates back to Brooks' time on the Memphis Grizzlies when he matched up against James and the Lakers in the first round of the 2023 NBA playoffs.

Brooks took his first shot at James after a chippy Game 2.

"I don't care—he's old. You know what I mean?" Brooks said after Memphis won Game 2. "I was waiting for that. I was expecting him to do that [in] Game 4, Game 5. He wanted to say something when I got my fourth foul. He should have been saying that earlier on. But I poke bears. I don't respect no one until they come and give me 40."

That quote, plus some of Brooks' antics on the court, sparked a years-long rivalry that hasn't seemed to slow down. Earlier this offseason, Brooks called himself James' "top" hater and told him to "stop all this waiting s--t" as James mulled his free agency decision.

With James getting closer and closer to retirement, it remains to be seen whether Brooks will lighten up when he goes up against the all-time great.

articles.title: Does Jonathan Kuminga Actually Make Sense for the Los Angeles Lakers?
articles.summary: On Wednesday, the Cleveland Cavaliers made news by trading for Peyton Watson, effectively taking themselves out of the mix for Jonathan Kuminga.
articles.body:
On Wednesday, the Cleveland Cavaliers made news by trading for Peyton Watson, effectively taking themselves out of the mix for Jonathan Kuminga.

According to reporting , that means the Los Angeles Lakers are now one of the two remaining suitors (along with the Minnesota Timberwolves) for the soon-to-be-24-year-old forward.

While L.A. could use an infusion of size and athleticism from Kuminga, it's fair to wonder whether he's worth what it might cost to land him.

He certainly won't want to take a pay cut, but the lack of spending power left around the NBA severely limits his options.

The Lakers can only offer Kuminga a minimum salary in free agency. A sign-and-trade may be his only viable path to any new team, since the Hawks can sign him to a deal starting at 120 percent of last season's $23.8 million salary.

At that price—and given that Atlanta would need sweeteners (like a young talent or draft assets)—the path feels a little less viable for the Lakers.

Los Angeles can get to around $18 million in tradable salary with Jarred Vanderbilt and Jake LaRavia, but Kuminga hasn't proven worth the depth a two-for-one deal would cost.

With averages of 12.5 points and 4.2 rebounds, Kuminga has been a solid, though unspectacular producer during his five seasons. He has a career 33.1 three-point percentage and has barely above-average scoring efficiency. He doesn't pass enough, either.

In fact, two teams have already voluntarily removed themselves from the Kuminga business (Golden State traded him, and Atlanta declined his 2026-27 team option). He'd be far from a lock for the Lakers' starting five.

But while Kuminga is still a roll of the dice, at least to some degree, that doesn't mean he wouldn't be worth it for the right price.

As we get deeper into this offseason, it should become clear to Kuminga and his representation that he simply won't command the payday they want. You'd think that might happen sooner rather than later, considering they had to go through this same dance last summer.

Regardless of the time frame, that realization has to come eventually.

When it does, L.A. may be able to orchestrate a sign-and-trade with the Hawks that starts Kuminga's next salary around the range of Vanderbilt's $12.4 million. Atlanta would still need a pick swap (or maybe a second-rounder or two), and there's certainly risk involved there. But that risk is a lot easier to take on when you're paying Kuminga like a reserve.

Though there are real concerns with his game, like the inconsistent shooting and lack of ancillary contributions, Kuminga has more upside than the 27-year-old garbage man Vanderbilt. And he's never shared the floor with a playmaker like Luka Dončić.

Again, Kuminga could very well come off the bench for L.A., but some of his minutes would certainly overlap with Luka's. In those lineups, while defenders are focused on Dončić and Austin Reaves (assuming he's on too), Kuminga could feast on the open looks created by those two inside.

One aspect of his potential that's never been properly emphasized is what Kuminga can be as a play finisher around the rim. He's spent far too many possessions trying to show off as a ball-handler and from-scratch scorer. He should be spending far more possessions as a cutter and lob finisher.

That shift would almost certainly take place with Luka. And at the right price, Kuminga wouldn't be the only one benefiting here.

Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton at least bring some defensive effort, but both are a little undersized for their positions. Kuminga hasn't exactly proved himself to be a lockdown defender in the NBA, but he's big, athletic and at least has more potential for versatility on that end than anyone currently on L.A.'s roster.

With the right, focused offensive role, buoyed by Luka and Reaves, Kuminga could be convinced to expend a little more on the less glamorous side of the court.

There's obviously a lot of "ifs, ands, buts" and other qualifications there. Really, that's true of this entire breakdown. But that's a product of the situation Kuminga has created for himself.

Ultimately, he's only worth it for the Lakers if he arrives in a reasonable deal.

But on the bright side for Kuminga, taking that reasonable deal now could put him in the best spot to earn more money later.

articles.title: Klay Thompson Calls Out 'Casuals' Over Ray Allen Debate, Cites Warriors Stats During NBA Title Runs
articles.summary: Klay Thompson defended himself in a debate amongst fans on social media on Thursday.
articles.body:
Klay Thompson defended himself in a debate amongst fans on social media on Thursday.

An Instagram post from the Swish List podcast was debating whether Thompson or Ray Allen is a better all-time player, and Thompson made his case against the legendary sharpshooter. Some fans were bringing up the two players' scoring numbers, which Thompson said were a reflection of how good their teams were.

"You do realize I was the second leading scorer on two championship teams without [Kevin Durant]? You want me to go to a bad team and put up empty stats, that's easy buddy," he commented on the post.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

He also pointed out his performance in the 2016 NBA Finals as fans downplayed his success with the Golden State Warriors.

"Holy s--t I led the 2016 playoffs in points scored you casuals," Thompson wrote.

Both Thompson and Allen were tremendous players in their primes, and both played a huge role on championship teams. Allen won a title with the Celtics and another with the Heat, while Thompson won four with Golden State.

It's a fair debate to have, but most NBA fans likely recognize that both players are among the best of their respective generations.

Thompson, perhaps getting some confidence with age, has had no problem responding to digs on social media this summer. Earlier this month, he called out his former teammate Kevin Durant when he said the current Philadelphia 76ers are better than his Warriors teams.

While most NBA players avoid discourse from fans on social media, Thompson has perhaps earned the right to defend his name after all the success he's had during his career.

The question now is how Thompson will continue adding to his legacy.

He recently said that he wants to "compete" for a title and "play a role on a team that can make a deep playoff run," and it's fair to say that the Mavs aren't exactly built to win a championship right now.

Thompson is under contract this season, but whether he'll request a trade remains to be seen.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Bueckers, Cunningham's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights as Wings Beat Fever
articles.summary: A pair of premier guards matched up on Thursday as Paige Bueckers and the Dallas Wings downed Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever 91-85.
articles.body:
A pair of premier guards matched up on Thursday as Paige Bueckers and the Dallas Wings downed Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever 91-85.

The Fever came in as 2.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but the Wings were looking to get a big win to improve their playoff position.

Bueckers had a bit of an off night, but luckily she had Jessica Sheppard and Arike Ogunbowale to lead the way for Dallas.

Clark likewise struggled a bit in the loss as she couldn't get much going on offense, but Kelsey Mitchell continued her tremendous season and kept the Fever alive for most of the night.

Dallas held a steady lead for most of the fourth quarter, but Indiana made a push in the final minutes. Ultimately, the Fever came up just short as the Wings were able to hold off the late run.

With the win, Dallas improved to 21-16 but still sits in eighth place in the WNBA standings. Luckily for the Wings, they're still sitting comfortably ahead of the ninth-place Portland Fire.

The Fever dropped to 24-13 with the loss and are now tied with the Las Vegas Aces for the third-best record in the league, but Indiana is closing in on clinching a playoff berth.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers Appears to Tell Caitlin Clark to 'Calm Down' in Trending Video of Heated Exchange
articles.summary: Things got heated between Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers during the Dallas Wings' win over the Indiana Fever on Thursday.
articles.body:
Things got heated between Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers during the Dallas Wings' win over the Indiana Fever on Thursday.

While Clark argued with an official about a call, Bueckers appeared to tell the Fever star to "calm down."

Clark perhaps let her frustration boil over during what was a rough showing from her. She finished with just 10 points on 10-of-15 from the field and 2-of-8 from deep, adding nine assists and four boards.

Bueckers also wasn't at her best as she had 13 points, eight assists and six rebounds on 5-of-16 from the field and 0-of-2 from deep, but the Wings managed to leave with a win thanks to 32 points from Arike Ogunbowale.

While Clark and Bueckers are both still young, they've each turned into two of the best guards in the league.

Clark is putting up 22.1 points and 8.3 assists per game this year, making a serious case to win her first MVP. Bueckers, who is in just her second season, is averaging 20.5 points, 5.8 assists and 4.1 rebounds per game.

Clark's Fever are sitting in third place in the WNBA standings at 24-13, tied with the Las Vegas Aces. Buckers' Wings are in eighth place at 21-16 but are in good playoff position, sitting five games ahead of the ninth-placed Portland Fire.

Thursday was the last matchup between Clark and Bueckers this season, but the two very well could meet again in the postseason.

articles.title: "Campazzo iba a 300 kilómetros por hora"
articles.standfirst: Ognjen Dobric recuerda el paso de Facundo Campazzo por el Estrella Roja antes de regresar al Real Madrid
articles.summary: Ognjen Dobric recuerda el paso de Facundo Campazzo por el Estrella Roja antes de regresar al Real Madrid
articles.body: Ognjen Dobric, capitán del Estrella Roja que esta temporada entrena el español Ibon Navarro y excompañero del Facundo Campazzo en el equipo de Belgrado la temporada 2022–2023, habló sobre el base del Real Madrid en el podcast '6.75range'. "Campazzo siempre estaba esprintando. Iba a 300 kilómetros por hora; nunca había visto algo así", compartió el escolta de 31 años sobre el base del Real Madrid. Dobric destacó que "Campazzo no se cansaba. Y Dusko Ivanovic (el entonces entrenador del Estrella Roja) ama a los jugadores así. Todos empezamos a alimentarnos de esa energía". "El mayor nombre del equipo llega y es el que más duro entrena. Te sientes estúpido si no trabajas. Y además sabe tanto de baloncesto… Sabe exactamente qué jugada marcar y cuándo. A quién atacar. Es un líder increíble. Nunca decía: "Dusko, lo hacemos a mi manera". Siempre respetaba", recuerda Dobric sobre el paso de Campazzo por el Estrella Roja. Facundo Campazzo llegó al Estrella Roja tras dejar la NBA, y en Serbia promedió 13 puntos y 6,5 asistencias en la Liga Adriática y 15 puntos y 5,9 asistencias en Euroliga. El 18 de julio de 2023 fichaba por el Real Madrid. Respecto a los métodos de trabajo de Ivanovic compartió que "Dusko es un hombre muy justo. Con él, te ganas los minutos en los entrenamientos. Si no entrenabas el día antes del partido, no jugabas. Si alguien estaba bien en el entrenamiento, jugaba veinte minutos. Todos lo sabían así que iban al máximo, recordó. Ognjen Dobric se atrevió a confeccionar un quinteto de los mejores jugadores extranjeros con los que coincidió en el Estrella Roja, y eligió de primeras a Facundo Campazzo, Jared Butler, Marco Belinelli, Tornike Shengelia y Bryant Dunston. "Vale, ahora necesito un 'cuatro'. Había nombres de todo tipo: Shengelia, Moneke, Johnny O'Bryant... ¿Te acuerdas de Johnny?. ¿Quién más estaba...? Nadie sabe dónde está Johnny O'Bryant. Cuando apareció, en la temporada del coronavirus—, el entrenador Dejo Radonjic lo había echado.Lo echó, pero cuando íbamos a la Copa en Novi Sad ahí estaba él, delante del autobús. Le pregunto: "¿Qué haces aquí?", y me dice: "Me llamaron para ir con vosotros". Lo habían echado, hermano; plena pandemia, nos faltaba un jugador. Lo llamaron, vino, cumplió con su trabajo, regresó de Novi Sad, aparcó frente al Pionir y nunca más lo volvimos a ver", recordó Ognjen Dobric entre risas.

articles.title: La historia de hermanamiento más bonita del deporte con el Partizán de Belgrado y el Fuenlabrada como protagonistas
articles.standfirst: El conjunto serbio aprovechó su partido con el Getafe de la Conference League para visitar el pabellón Fernando Martín de baloncesto
articles.summary: El conjunto serbio aprovechó su partido con el Getafe de la Conference League para visitar el pabellón Fernando Martín de baloncesto
articles.body: Hay historias en el mundo del deporte que merecen ser contadas una y otra vez sin que uno se canse de escucharlas y disfrutarlas por asombrosas que son y por la repercusión emocional y deportiva que tienen. Y una de esas historias la protagonizan el Baloncesto Fuenlabrada y el Partizán de Belgrado. La historia de hermanamiento entre el conjunto del Sur de Madrid y el serbio nació la temporada 91-92, cuando en plena guerra de los Balcanes, el Partizán encontró cobijo en Fuenlabrada para disputar sus partidos de Euroliga en el Fernando Martín fuenlabreño, haciendo de la localidad madrileña un pequeño barrio serbio en el que encontró una afición que le llevó en volandas hacia el título europeo. Años más tarde ese hermanamiento sigue alimentándose y poniéndose de manifiesto cada vez que hay oportunidad, de hecho en los próximos días los de Iñaki Martín viajarán hasta Belgrado para disputar un amistoso de pretemporada donde son siempre recibidos con los brazos abiertos y con un cariño inimaginable haciendo de su visita a tierras serbias una ocasión perfecta para volver a celebrar aquella Euroliga.  Es tal la amistad entre ambos equipos y aficiones que aprovechando el partido de previa de la Conference League entre el Getafe y el Partizán de Belgrado que se disputó en el Coliseum, los ultras serbios quisieron aprovechar el viaje y peregrinar hasta Fuenlabrada, a escasos kilómetros de donde se disputaba su partido de fútbol, para visitar el Fernando Martín, pabellón donde hace más de treinta años se sintieron como en casa dejando claro una vez más que la historia entre el Baloncesto Fuenlabrada y el Partizán de Belgrado va más allá del básket, el fútbol o cualquier otra cosa, va de hermanamiento y de agradecimiento.

articles.title: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert Says Others Are Trying to 'Sow Divisiveness' in Transgender Debate
articles.summary: DALLAS (AP) — WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert denounced people she said are trying to "sow divisiveness" as the league grapples with a debate over transgender athletes.
articles.body:
DALLAS (AP) — WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert denounced people she said are trying to "sow divisiveness" as the league grapples with a debate over transgender athletes.

Engelbert made the comments Thursday before the Indiana Fever's 91-85 loss to the Dallas Wings at the home of the Dallas Mavericks.

Demonstrators showed up outside American Airlines Center, as they have at other venues since the Fever's Sophie Cunningham voiced support for barring transgender girls and women from girls' and women's sports in an extensive ESPN profile.

Source: Freedom, White Not Eligible for WNBA Draft (AP)

Sky Ban Enes Kanter Freedom from Home Games (AP)

The league issued a statement last week criticizing efforts to make an issue about the eligibility of transgender athletes in the WNBA. Engelbert's comments in a pregame gathering in Dallas were her first since the league called out what it said were bad faith efforts to use the debate to "demean or marginalize others."

"People are trying to use the league to sow divisiveness," Engelbert said Thursday while sitting alongside Wings CEO and managing partner Greg Bibb.

"We're being the center of political football for people who have never watched the WNBA, never have written about the WNBA or reported on the WNBA," Engelbert said, echoing NBA Commissioner Adam Silver's recent use of "political football" to describe the debate that has engulfed the WNBA.

The league's collective bargaining agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA," but it does not include any more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth. Earlier this month, two former NBA players, Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White, declared themselves eligible for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women.

Engelbert sent a memo this month to team presidents and general managers saying the league would discuss the subject of transgender women in women's basketball.

"There's always going to be haters out there and we denounce it," Engelebert said Thursday. "But that's what happens when you have made it as a legitimate sports media and entertainment product."

articles.title: Jury Says The New York Times Defamed Alabama Basketball Player with Incorrect Story About Shooting
articles.summary: TUSCALOOSA, Ala. (AP) — An Alabama jury on Thursday awarded $9.25 million in damages after finding that The New York Times defamed a college basketball player by incorrectly reporting that he was at the scene of a fatal shooting in Tuscaloosa.
articles.body:
TUSCALOOSA, Ala. (AP) — An Alabama jury on Thursday awarded $9.25 million in damages after finding that The New York Times defamed a college basketball player by incorrectly reporting that he was at the scene of a fatal shooting in Tuscaloosa.

Kai Spears, who played for the University of Alabama men's team, sued the Times in 2023 after it published a report , citing a person familiar with the investigation, that indicated he was a passenger in a car involved in the shooting. The Times reported that the person had spoken "on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive matters."

Days later, the Times acknowledged its error in an editor's note and corrected the story.

The eight-person jury delivered its verdict after a nine-day trial in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Alabama. Matt Glover, an attorney for Spears, said he was pleased with the decision and believes "this verdict will improve journalism throughout the country."

The Times was reviewing its legal options after losing in court, spokesperson Charlie Stadtlander said.

"We're disappointed the jury found The Times liable for an honest mistake," Stadtlander said in a statement Thursday. "We thank the jury for its service, but believe the verdict and award of damages are contrary to law and not supported by the evidence."

Three other basketball players from the school were present at the January 2023 shooting , which killed a 23-year-old mother. In the lawsuit, Spears claimed the inaccurate reporting had caused him emotional distress and forever linked him with a murder.

A Times article reporting on the verdict Thursday said the newspaper "had not lost a defamation lawsuit brought in the United States over one of its articles in more than 50 years."

articles.title: Is GG Banks Really Worth the Hype? Grading Every Aspect of the High School Phenom's Game
articles.summary: You might've seen the 17-year-old drilling shots alongside Shakira Austin and Elena Delle Donne at last month's WNBA All-Star Shooting Stars competition. Or maybe you've seen the viral clips of a shifty guard putting defenders in a blender at Overtime Select.
articles.body:
You might've seen the 17-year-old drilling shots alongside Shakira Austin and Elena Delle Donne at last month's WNBA All-Star Shooting Stars competition. Or maybe you've seen the viral clips of a shifty guard putting defenders in a blender at Overtime Select .

Well, that's GG Banks, a rising senior who is ranked No. 4 in the 2027 recruiting class. There's a lot of hype surrounding her, but just how good of a prospect is Banks?

I went through her film to break down every part of her game, from her athleticism and pick-and-roll playmaking to the shooting, defense and everything in between. Also, since she's only 17, a lot can change over the next few years, so there's plenty of upside baked into these grades.

When you watch Banks' film, it doesn't take long to realize just how ridiculous of an athlete she is. Guards who move like this don't exactly grow on trees.

She's incredibly explosive, but it's the combination of her speed, flexibility and change of direction that's really special. Banks can get downhill in a hurry, change speeds on a dime without losing much momentum and maneuver through tight spaces in ways most players can't.

That athleticism is especially dangerous in transition. Once Banks gets out in the open court, she covers ground in an instant before blowing past defenders. There's no question she will be one of the best transition scorers in college basketball.

And then there's the physical profile. Banks is listed on most sites at 5'8", but she has a 6'0" wingspan, which is significantly longer than most guards at her size. That length shows up when Banks is finishing with arms fully extended around the rim, but it also helps her make plays in passing lanes defensively.

Advantage creation is the name of the game at the point guard position. The best of them constantly put pressure on the defense, whether that's forcing help to come over off the drive or drawing two to the ball in pick-and-roll. That ability is one of the most impressive parts of Banks' game.

She has unbelievable feel for creating out of ball screens, and a lot of that starts with her handle. Banks is extremely creative with the ball, using inside-out dribbles, hesitations and left-right crossovers to keep defenders off balance. She loves to use her outside foot to sell defenders in one direction, then drive the other way.

Once you combine her improvisational skills with top-tier burst and acceleration, she's almost impossible to keep out of the paint. She gets to the rim so quickly she's consistently forcing weak-side defenders to help over, which leads to a lot of free throws and opens up things for her as a passer, too.

If you just watch Banks' highlights, one of the first things that jumps out is how impressive her gathers and high-difficulty finishes are. She has an incredible ability to contort her body around defenders to create openings. But sometimes, that creativity is a little too much.

Banks will often have a relatively easy layup available, only to make the finish much harder than it needs to be. Some of that comes down to her biggest improvement area: the left hand. At the high school level, Banks is so athletic and so skilled with the ball, she can get away with exclusively finishing with her strong hand right now. That won't always be the case at higher levels.

On the passing front, Banks is unsurprisingly really creative. She is a high-risk, high-reward passer, who attempts passes most players wouldn't even see. She consistently uses her eyes to manipulate defenders in ball screens and isn't afraid of making tight window passes.

Similar to all-world creators like Caitlin Clark and Olivia Miles, this style leads to a lot of assists but a good amount of turnovers as well. Across 16 games at 17U Nike EYBL, Banks averaged the third-most assists (5.5) and second-most turnovers (4.6) on the circuit.

The biggest question when it comes to Banks' on-ball operation is whether she can become a consistent shooter.

Right now, the three-point numbers just aren't there. She shot just 24 percent from three at 17U and 13.6 percent (3-of-22) across 5 games at Overtime Select, a league featuring the top high school players in the country.

One mechanical thing that stands out is the deep knee bend when she shoots. It can slow down her release, and at times, you'll see it cause her to leave shots short—especially off the dribble. The upper body mechanics aren't always compact, either.

Banks also attempted just one pull-up three (a miss) with Team USA at the U18 AmeriCup in June. Though, she did shoot 37.5 percent on catch-and-shoot threes (3-of-8), which were mostly all uncontested.

According to an article by On3's Hunter Shelton , Banks said her midrange game is one of the areas she's working hardest to improve.

If Banks can become even a reliable shooter, it changes the equation completely. Opponents already have to respect her first step and ability to get to the rim at-well. If she can punish them for going under screens with a consistent jumper, even more things will open up for her offensively—on and off the ball.

There's a lot of upside with Banks defensively, but there's definitely some inconsistency right now. Her footwork navigating screens can get a little choppy, and there are possessions where she simply isn't as engaged as you'd like.

But when she's locked in, you can see the flashes she has as a really disruptive defender. Banks' hands are extremely active, and she does a good job using her athleticism and length to get into passing lanes and create turnovers. She averaged 3.3 steals per game at 17U, which ranked second on the circuit.

The next step is to be more consistent on a possession-by-possession basis, but this isn't an unusual issue for a high-usage offensive creator at the high-school level. Banks has the athletic tools and a plus-wingspan; it's just about dialing in on the details.

The easy comparison for Banks is LSU's MiLaysia Fulwiley, particularly with their athletic profiles and process creating off the bounce.

Both are explosive, creative guards who put a ton of pressure on the rim with their athleticism and handle. They have that improvisational ability to make something out of seemingly nothing.

Fulwiley and Banks also have similar questions as prospects. Neither players are consistent shooters, and both struggle to use their left hand consistently.

At the WNBA level, there's some overlap with Portland's Carla Leite, in terms of their ability to dominate a game in ball screens and live in the paint. Also imagine if Seattle's Jade Melbourne had a better handle; that's sort of the idea here.

The ideal system for Banks is up-tempo offense that puts her in a lot of ball screens, surrounds her with shooting and gives her plenty of space to attack downhill. The more she can get the ball in hands with a runway to the rim, the more you actualize her athleticism and creativity.

Banks has interest from schools across the country, but according to an interview with CBS Sports' Isabel Gonzalez , Texas, LSU, South Carolina and Ohio State are the programs she's hearing from the most.

Here's how those four teams ranked in Barrtorvik's adjusted tempo metric last season: LSU (No. 7), Ohio State (No. 20), Texas (No. 104) and South Carolina (No. 115).

LSU and Ohio State are probably the best contexts for her to play the style of game she's best at, while spending four years at South Carolina would likely get the most out of her defensively, as an off-ball player and in the weight room.

Texas is the one fit that makes the least sense. They play at a slower pace, rely heavily on midrange pull-ups and generally don't create the kind of spacing that would allow Banks to flourish as a driver. And considering shooting is already one of the biggest questions in her game, I'm not sure that environment would put her in the best position to develop.

articles.title: Angel Reese Makes WNBA History, Final Box Score Stats, Highlights as Dream Beat Brink, Sparks
articles.summary: Angel Reese's perfect shooting night helped the Atlanta Dream cruise to an easy 124-88 win over the Los Angeles Sparks on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Angel Reese's perfect shooting night helped the Atlanta Dream cruise to an easy 124-88 win over the Los Angeles Sparks on Thursday night.

The Dream, who entered the night favored by 8.5 points at FanDuel Sportsbook , had no problem covering en route to earning their fourth win in the last five games.

Reese became the first player in WNBA history to have a game with at least 20 points, 10 rebounds, five assists and three steals without missing a shot from the field.

Reese joined Nikola Jokić as the only players in NBA and WNBA history have that stat line. Jokić did it during the 2018-19 season when he had 35 points on 11-of-11 shooting, 11 rebounds, 11 assists and four steals for the Denver Nuggets in a win over the Phoenix Suns.

A segment of Reese's night included going on a personal 10-0 run against the Sparks defense in the second quarter. The Dream led by as many as 42 points at one point. Their 124 points tied the second-highest output by any team this season.

Per the Associated Press , Reese is the third player in WNBA history with a 20-point double-double without a missed field goal. She also set the Dream record for most field-goals without a miss in a game.

Reese also recorded her league-leading 25th double-double of the season in the process. Dallas Wings forward Jessica Shepard is the only other player with 20 double-doubles.

The win moved Atlanta (23-13) one-half game behind the Indiana Fever for the No. 4 seed and homecourt advantage in the first round of the playoffs with eight games remaining in the regular season.

Next up for Reese and the Dream is a matchup with the Phoenix Mercury on Saturday at Mortgage Matchup Center.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball Trade Talks Revealed by Hornets in New Behind-the-Scenes Video from NBA Free Agency
articles.summary: Two months after one of the most surprising trades of the NBA offseason, the Charlotte Hornets have provided an inside look into the process that led to them dealing LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves.
articles.body:
Two months after one of the most surprising trades of the NBA offseason, the Charlotte Hornets have provided an inside look into the process that led to them dealing LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

In a "Reel Access" video on their YouTube channel (starts at 10:43 mark), Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson and the front office are seen deliberating about a proposal from an unnamed team that is "meeting our price" on Ball.

Later in the video (starts at 24:05), after the Hornets and Timberwolves have agreed to the deal, front-office personnel are shown explaining that they need to reach out to the parties involved in the trade to ensure they hear about it from them before it breaks publicly.

It's also notable at one point Peterson says the Hornets were "probably" trading Miles Bridges if they dealt Ball.

The full terms of the trade were Ball and Josh Green going to Minnesota in exchange for Naz Reid, an unprotected first-round pick in 2033, three first-round pick swaps in 2028, 2029 and 2030, and three second-round picks in 2029, 2032 and 2033.

Bridges wound up getting moved in a separate deal to the Phoenix Suns in which Charlotte also sent out a 2029 first-round pick and a 2027 second-round pick. The Hornets got back Grayson Allen, Royce O'Neale and a 2033 first-round pick.

Trading Ball, in particular, was a stunner for a Hornets team that showed tremendous promise down the stretch last season when he played alongside Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miler.

Charlotte went 18-7 over its final 25 regular-season games, which is roughly a 59-win pace over 82 games. Even factoring in some of that success was inflated by playing teams that were tanking down the stretch, it did suggest the franchise was trending in the right direction.

Now, the Hornets have indicated they plan to move forward with Knueppel and Miller as their key pieces for the 2026-27 season. Ball gets a fresh start to show what he can do playing alongside a strong No. 1 option with the Timberwolves in Anthony Edwards.

Ball will play his first game back in Charlotte as a visiting player on Feb. 15 when the Timberwolves take on the Hornets at the Spectrum Center.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Reacts to NBA 2K27 Player Rating in New Video After Trade to 76ers from Celtics
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown had some qualms with 2K after his player rating in NBA 2K27 was revealed.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown had some qualms with 2K after his player rating in NBA 2K27 was revealed.

Brown said he was "offended" that his mid-range rating was only a 90 since he is a "spammer" in that area of the court, and he also questioned how his overall rating dropped two points to 91 after being 93 last year.

It is a bit hard to justify Brown's overall rating going down when he just finished sixth in MVP voting. Even with all of the handwringing over his efficiency, he was the main piece for a Boston Celtics team that won 56 games last season.

Brown will be bringing his 91 overall rating to the Sixers after a surprise trade with Boston in the offseason. He is part of a new-look Philadelphia roster that also added LeBron James to play alongside Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe.

articles.title: James Harden's Pay Cut, Peyton Watson Recruitment Detailed in New NBA Rumors After Cavs Contract
articles.summary: Veteran guard James Harden was reportedly both flexible and influential during the Cleveland Cavaliers' pursuit of Peyton Watson.
articles.body:
Veteran guard James Harden was reportedly both flexible and influential during the Cleveland Cavaliers' pursuit of Peyton Watson.

In the wake of the Cavs acquiring Watson from the Denver Nuggets this week, ESPN NBA insider Brian Windhorst provided some insight into Harden's role in the process on Friday's episode of Brian Windhorst & The Hoop Collective (beginning at the 12-minute mark) .

"James Harden was willing to opt out of that contract and sit around all summer, and basically pick up the phone whenever the Cavs called and say, 'Yeah, I'll go down a little farther. I'll go down a little farther,'" Windhorst said. "So as the Cavs made various moves, Harden was not only willing to reduce his salary, but he was willing to recruit. He—from what I understand—he recruited Peyton Watson."

The Watson deal was agreed upon Wednesday, as the Cavs sent Max Strus to the Los Angeles Clippers and an unprotected 2031 first-round pick to the Nuggets as part of the three-team trade.

One day later, Harden's agents informed ESPN's Shams Charania that Harden had agreed to a three-year, $97 million contract to return to the Cavaliers.

It was considered a foregone conclusion throughout the offseason that Harden would re-sign with the Cavs, but he waited and allowed the organization to pursue other potential upgrades to the roster.

LeBron James' agent, Rich Paul, confirmed on his Game Over podcast (h/t Conor Smith of the Philadelphia Inquirer ) that the Cavs were among the finalists in the LeBron sweepstakes before he decided to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers.

Had James chosen the Cavs, it would have marked his third stint with the organization he led to a championship in 2016.

Despite LeBron going elsewhere, Harden remained patient, and it paid off in the form of Cleveland adding Watson to the team's already impressive core of Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Mitchell.

Watson set career highs with 14.6 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 three-pointers made per game last season, and adding him to a Cavs team that reached the Eastern Conference Finals last season should make Cleveland an even more serious contender in 2026-27.

articles.title: Marc Stad Buys Majority Stake in T-Wolves, Lynx at $4.5B Valuation in Deal with Marc Lore
articles.summary: Two years after Marc Lore took over as majority owner and governor of the Minnesota Timberwolves, he has sold most of his interest in the NBA franchise as well as the WNBA's Minnesota Lynx.
articles.body:
Two years after Marc Lore took over as majority owner and governor of the Minnesota Timberwolves, he has sold most of his interest in the NBA franchise as well as the WNBA's Minnesota Lynx.

Per ESPN's Shams Charania, Marc Stad will take over as controlling owner of the T-Wolves and Lynx after buying a majority of Lore's interest at a $4.5 billion valuation.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

MLB legend Alex Rodriguez, who was part of the group that purchased the Timberwolves and Lynx with Lore, issued a statement Friday saying he will be increasing his investment in the team.

"One of the great joys I've had in my career is spending the last few years helping build the Timberwolves and Lynx with my friend and partner Marc Lore," Rodriguez said.

"I'm very excited to announce that this incredible journey reaches a new level today. Marc and Elisa Stad, who have been our partners and friends since we bought the teams, will be increasing their investment and joining me as Co-Chairman. I will also be increasing my investment and spending even more time with the teams as Co-Chairman, Governor of the Lynx, and alternate Governor of the Timberwolves, pending league approval. While Marc Lore will be reducing his role and ownership to focus on his business, he remains an investor and a key part of our partnership. I could not be more energized about this evolution and what we're all going to do together for the Twin Cities."

The Timberwolves sale marks the ninth time an NBA franchise has been sold since 2022, including the deal that saw Lore and Rodriguez purchase Minnesota from Glen Taylor.

It was less than two weeks ago that Mark Walter agreed to sell the Los Angeles Lakers to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner at a $12.5 billion valuation. Walter's purchase of the franchise had just been approved by the NBA board of governors in October 2025.

Other NBA franchises that have been sold during this period include the Phoenix Suns, Dallas Mavericks, Charlotte Hornets, Boston Celtics and Portland Trail Blazers.

The Lore-Rodriguez purchase of the Timberwolves was officially approved by the NBA in June 2025. Their approval came after a prolonged battle with Taylor, who said in March 2024 that Lore and Rodriguez lost the financial backing needed to make their final payment required to claim majority ownership of the franchise.

Lore and Rodriguez faced questions about their long-term financial ability to maintain a competitive NBA roster. Adrian Wojnarowski, then of ESPN, reported in April 2024 that part of Taylor's concern with selling to them was a budget projection for the 2024-25 season from Lore and Rodriguez that would have cut $27 million in payroll to get under the luxury tax.

In the lone season with Lore and Rodriguez as controlling owners, the Timberwolves had the third-highest payroll in the NBA.

Forbes noted Stad's investment group manages over $35 billion in capital, though his specific net worth is not mentioned in the article.

The Timberwolves have made the playoffs in five consecutive seasons, making the Western Conference Finals in 2024 and 2025. They finished last season as the No. 6 seed in the West and upset the Denver Nuggets in the first round before losing to the San Antonio Spurs in the conference semifinals.

articles.title: NCAA Gets Win In Court On 5-Year Eligibility Rule, But This Is Hardly the End Of the Lawsuits
articles.summary: DENVER (AP) — The NCAA notched an important win in federal court Friday over its much-disputed five-year eligibility rule, though it fell short of shutting down the last-minute shuffling threatening to upend college sports rosters with football season fast approaching.
articles.body:
DENVER (AP) — The NCAA notched an important win in federal court Friday over its much-disputed five-year eligibility rule, though it fell short of shutting down the last-minute shuffling threatening to upend college sports rosters with football season fast approaching.

A 2-1 decision by a panel of the U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals halted, for now, a judge's order that would have granted thousands of athletes an extra season of eligibility. But it did nothing to resolve dozens of other lawsuits and court orders piling up across the country that allow players in the same situation to join teams for the upcoming season.

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

Virtually all these lawsuits involve players who graduated from high school in 2022, whose college eligibility ended last season and who were not included in the NCAA's controversial new rule — less than two months old — that grants most Division I athletes five years of eligibility over five years but doesn't take effect until next season.

"There's a reason we saw so many state-court lawsuits filed" after the now-paused federal court ruling that came down July 31, said Sam Ehrlich, a former lawyer who now works at Boise State and operates the College Sports Litigation Tracker. "It was a 'just in case.' They did it just in case what we just saw happen actually happened."

Among the many athletes watching this unfold and wondering where it winds up are defensive linemen Kellan Wyatt and Stephan Daley, both members of the national championship team at Indiana last season who decided to return after the lower-court decision. So are former Ole Miss starters Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris and Wydett Williams, who won a ruling from a Louisiana state court giving them another season of eligibility even though they had signed with NFL teams this summer.

While some players hope to land back at their schools, whatever the impact on the rosters, how that works isn't at all clear in many cases. The judge in the case involving the Ole Miss players, for example, gave them a week to enter the transfer portal, which for football players is only open in January.

In appealing the state court cases, the NCAA is expected to invoke parts of Friday's ruling, which agreed with NCAA arguments that it was likely to win the case when it's heard in full — probably several months from now — and that the NCAA would suffer more harm than the players if the court didn't pause the order.

The NCAA can also take heart in an Ohio appeals court that paused a similar injunction involving Xavier basketball Filip Borovicanin and others.

But other than those two cases, Ehrlich said, judges across the country "are unanimous that the NCAA is in the wrong" on the five-year eligibility issue when it comes to the Class of 2022.

Plaintiffs' attorney Rob Shelquist issued a statement calling the appeals court ruling procedural and "not a decision on the merits of the athletes' antitrust claims."

"We are exploring every available option given the split in the panel's ruling and remain committed to fighting for these college athletes whose opportunities and eligibility have been unfairly restricted," he said.

The NCAA's chief legal officer, Scott Bearby, sent a memo to schools telling them they would not be subject to NCAA punishment for allowing any player to compete between the time the July 31 ruling came down and Friday. But he reiterated that those players are no longer eligible.

Bearby also acknowledged that the NCAA would continue to defend lawsuits around the country — a signal that the NCAA knows Friday's ruling offers no guarantees of an end to the roster chaos.

"If anything, I do wonder if there's a part of the NCAA that's, like, 'Maybe we'd have been better off not getting the stay because, boy, there's going to be a lot of lawsuits filed over the next couple of weeks,'" Ehrlich said.

Courts that go beyond filing emergency injunctions and take up the cases in their entirety will have to decide who suffers more harm: Is it players who can't play a fifth year and could lose educational and NIL opportunities? Or incoming freshmen who signed with the idea that they wouldn't be competing against a class of fifth-year seniors?

When the NCAA decided to have the rule kick in next year, it also grappled with that calculation, knowing it couldn't be perfectly fair.

"Fairness is in the eye of the beholder," the NCAA argued in its legal brief in the appeals case. "Countless student-athletes already on campuses, and schools who built their rosters in reliance on the rules the NCAA's membership wrote and agreed to follow, do not believe it is fair for thousands of formerly ineligible athletes to return to competition at the start of the 2026–27 season."

articles.title: Los Wolves cambian de dueño por 4.500 millones de dólares
articles.standfirst: Segunda venta de un equipo de la NBA en menos de un mes
articles.summary: Segunda venta de un equipo de la NBA en menos de un mes
articles.body: El empresario Marc Stad alcanzó un acuerdo para comprar los Minnesota Timberwolves y las Minnesota Lynx por 4.500 millones de dólares, según anunció este viernes la cadena ESPN. Stad, fundador del grupo inversor Dragoneer Investment Group, era hasta la fecha un socio minoritario en ambas franquicias, pero acordó la compra de la participación mayoritaria del empresario Marc Lore. Lore ejercía como copresidente de los dos equipos de la NBA y la WNBA junto con el exjugador de béisbol Álex Rodríguez, quien continuará en su cargo actual. Esta es la segunda venta de una franquicia de la NBA en el último mes, después de que el dueño de Los Ángeles Lakers, Mark Walter, alcanzara el 12 de agosto un acuerdo para vender la franquicia angelina a los empresarios Josh Kushner y Bob Iger por 12.000 millones de dólares. La venta de los Timberwolves y las Lynx es la cuarta operación más alta en la historia de la NBA. Además de la ya mencionada venta de los Lakers a Kushner e Iger, la franquicia angelina pasó a manos de Walter el año pasado tras comprarla por cerca de 10.000 millones de dólares a la familia Buss, propietaria de los angelinos desde 1979. Los eternos rivales del equipo de oro y púrpura, los Boston Celtics, también cambiaron de propietario hace un año a cambio de 6.100 millones de dólares.

articles.title: Los terremotos impiden al Granada jugar en su pabellón
articles.standfirst: Tiene que disputar en Córdoba su primer amistoso ante el Cajasol Coto
articles.summary: Tiene que disputar en Córdoba su primer amistoso ante el Cajasol Coto
articles.body: El enjambre sísmico que sufre Granada ha motivado que no se puedan disputar partidos en el Palacio de los Deportes de la capital al tener que realizarse labores de mantenimiento en sus gradas, por lo que el choque de la Copa Andalucía de la próxima semana entre Covirán Granada y Cajasol Coto Córdoba se jugará finalmente en tierras cordobesas. El Covirán Granada informó este viernes en un comunicado de que, "tras la evaluación realizada" en el Palacio de Deportes granadino "después de la serie de terremotos registrada en la provincia durante los últimos días, se deben llevar a cabo labores de mantenimiento en la grada del recinto". Esto ha llevado a la Federación Andaluza de Baloncesto a trasladar a Córdoba la sede del partido entre el Covirán Granada y el Cajasol Coto Córdoba correspondiente a la Copa de Andalucía y que se iba a disputar la próxima semana en Granada. El club rojinegro ya ha comunicado que "procederá a la devolución del importe de las entradas que ya habían sido adquiridas por los aficionados para el partido". El duelo andaluz se disputará el miércoles a las ocho de la tarde en el Palacio de Deportes Vista Alegre de Córdoba. Los terremotos llevaron al Covirán Granada a suspender sus entrenamientos previstos en las jornadas del martes, el miércoles y el jueves, mientras que el equipo dirigido por Arturo Ruiz ya se ejercita con normalidad desde este viernes pese a que el enjambre sísmico sigue afectando a Granada capital y su área metropolitana con continuos temblores.

articles.title: WNBA Stars Sophie Cunningham, StudBudz, More Reveal What They Bought with Massive New Contracts
articles.summary: WNBA players are enjoying more financial freedom after agreeing to a new collective bargaining agreement in March, and that means treating themselves a little bit even if many are saving and investing.
articles.body:
WNBA players are enjoying more financial freedom after agreeing to a new collective bargaining agreement in March, and that means treating themselves a little bit even if many are saving and investing.

ESPN's Kareem Copeland reported Friday players saw an average increase in pay of 366 percent with their first contracts this season and then relayed what some of them said they bought with their new money.

Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham purchased a VRBO in Arizona and explained she plans on expanding that business plan.

"I'm about to probably buy one in Nashville and Florida, and so I'm just starting to make a business outside of the court," Cunningham said. "It's good, it's fun. I'm trying to buy places that I want to go visit, so when I'm there, I don't have to pay for it.

"I think it's a long time coming, but now you have to be smart with that money. You can't just go out and blow it all or not invest. I think it allows all of us to kind of grow and be businesswomen."

Others took a different approach, including Minnesota Lynx guard Courtney Williams.

"I went to the strip club and blew a bag," Williams said. "No, I'm being dead serious. Like, that particular strip club will never see me for the rest of my life. Like, I did too much in there.

"Man, they probably know me by my name."

Williams and Seattle Storm guard Natisha Hiedeman are collectively known as "StudBudz," and the latter bought Williams a customized, seven-foot statue of the anime character Goku for her birthday.

"I ain't gonna lie, I spent a little bit on that," Hiedeman said. "They had to make it, ship it, do everything.

"She been saying she wanted one ... and she's putting her little crib together. But we said we're done buying each other expensive gifts now. So, that was her last gift from me."

Elsewhere, Washington Mystics forward Kiki Iriafen bought a black Porsche Cayenne coupe, Indiana Fever guard Lexie Hull bought a Tesla and Atlanta Dream forward Rhyne Howard bought a new Louis Vuitton bag.

"I definitely saved a lot of my money, invested a lot of money," Iriafen said. "I finally did my 401[k] this year. I did not do that last year, so I was really proud of myself for doing that.

That seemed to be a theme with many of the players investing but also enjoying a splurge, which is not surprising after they worked so hard during negotiations for the new CBA.

articles.title: Otro recital de España para meterse en la gran final
articles.standfirst: La selección femenina sub 16 luchará por el oro este sábado (19.30) ante Eslovenia
articles.summary: La selección femenina sub 16 luchará por el oro este sábado (19.30) ante Eslovenia
articles.body: La selección española femenina sub 16 ya está en la final del Eurobasket. Era lo más probable dado el camino que había seguido hasta la semifinal. Tras cinco partidos llegaba al duelo ante Letonia con una media de anotación de 110,8 puntos y cinco triunfos por una ventaja media de 79,2. Un abuso en toda regla de un equipo que borda el baloncesto. Aunque Letonia fue el rival que más complicaciones dio al combinado que entrena Madelen Urieta, las bálticas también cayeron con cierto estrépito en una semifinal dominada por España (91-53). Un resultado que vuelve a sorprender y deja clara la calidad del equipo de España femenino sub 16. Letonia tenía claro el plan. No dejar a España correr y parar su ritmo con faltas. De hecho en el primer cuarto más igualado que ha jugado el combinado español (15-14), las de Urrieta fueron 20 veces a la línea de personal, fallando 11 de esos tiros. Además España tuvo problemas desde el triple, 0/9 iniciado el segundo cuarto. Pero la igualdad se acabó dos minutos después de comenzar el segundo acto. A 8:42 para el final Letonia se puso por delante, 15-16... y el partido se acabó. De ahí al final del cuarto España engrasó su maquinaria, mejoró la defensa y corrió, para arrollar a su rival. Un primer parcial de 12-0 que luego fue de 23-2 (38-18) abría de par en par la puerta de la final para España. Al descanso se llegó con 46-22 que dejaba el partido casi liquidado. España no bajó su ritmo en la reanudación elevando su ventaja sobre un equipo letón que se acabó entregando a la superioridad española. Amelia Alonso acabó con un doble-doble (16 puntos y 10 rebotes), Paula Reynal hizo 15+8, Aisha Mbengue aportó 12 pntos y Anastasia Lishchuk logró un 9+8. España buscará el oro, que sería el segundo consecutivo y el duodécimo en total, este sábado a partir de las 19.30 ante Eslovenia que se cargó a Francia en la otra semifinal, 58-67. En ese partido la pintura tendrá una batalla de apeliidos ilustres con Anastasia, hija de Sergei Lishchuk, ante Ema, hija de Erazem Lorbek.
